View image in fullscreen Bayer Leverkusen players and fans hold a minute of silence for Peter Hermann. Photograph: Martin Meissner/AP

Never before had a team scored three times in successive Bundesliga home games and lost both of them but Borussia Mönchengladbach are managing to find a ledge beneath the edge. Gladbach made a bright start against Mainz (who are under interim coach Jan-Moritz Lichte) – with Florian Neuhaus scoring the opener on his return to the line-up, his first since May 2024 – but ended in defeat again, leaving them bottom, without a point. Alexander Blessin, a former St Pauli coach famed for his defensive work, is expected to arrive in an attempt to plug the leaks.

Hamburg had gone into matchday four pointless and goalless but managed to squeeze past a Köln side who dominated them, with Yussuf Poulsen’s second goal for the club since arriving in summer 2025 proving decisive. It was an endorsement of their faith in head coach Merlin Polzin, who signed a contract extension this week despite that bad start and successive 5-0 defeats.

There are comebacks and there are comebacks, and several coincided on the Weser as Werder Bremen continued their surprisingly good start to the season. They trailed 2-0 to Augsburg but were level after a Niclas Füllkrug netbuster but even better was around the corner, with Mitchell Weiser rattling in a perfect left-foot winner, deep into stoppage time, in his first home appearance after 16 months out with injury. It brought the former Bayern man to tears and his coach Daniel Thoune described it as “a goosebump moment”.

All three promoted teams now have a win after Paderborn’s shock victory over Hoffenheim in Sunday’s late game, with veteran substitute Steffen Tigges sealing it with a header for his first top-flight goal since 2024. It was a third loss in four for Hoffenheim, who also suffered an embarrassing Europa League reverse at OFI Crete on Thursday.

Sports.title: Pierre Sage took Lens to new heights. His replacement left after six games
Sports.content:
It was under cover of darkness that Yannick Cahuzac took his place in the Lens dugout at the Stade Louis II on Friday night. The lights dimmed as the players made their entrance and Cahuzac, who had been named interim manager just three days earlier, sat alone, leaning forward on a seat that Dino Toppmöller would have occupied if not for a dramatic turn of events last week.

Cahuzac’s appointment, much like his entrance in Monaco, had a stealthy quality, as if he had always been there and the switching of the lights was mere confirmation of his presence. Cahuzac left Lorient, where he had been Olivier Pantaloni’s assistant, at the end of last season to return to Lens, where he had finished his playing career before working as Franck Haise’s assistant in the 2022–23 campaign.

He was spoken about as a future No 1, but that was not the role he took in the summer. Cahuzac is still an apprentice who has not yet obtained his coaching qualifications so he returned to the club as an assistant to Toppmöller. The German had the unenviable task of succeeding Pierre Sage, who hastily departed to Crystal Palace after guiding Lens to a maiden Coupe de France triumph and a second-place finish in Ligue 1 last season.

Lens were not expected to soar as high this season. Speaking in the summer, the club’s sporting director, Jean-Louis Leca, said they were “not a Champions League club” and that an eighth-place finish in Ligue 1 would represent success. Toppmöller’s first game in charge brought silverware as Lens beat PSG in the Trophée des Champions; his first Ligue 1 game was a resounding 5-2 win over Auxerre; and his side took all three points away to Slavia Prague in their first Champions League game – not a bad start after a summer of upheaval and the departure of several important players.

Results have dipped in recent weeks but expectations were being met. Hence the shock last week when it was announced that the German had left the club by mutual consent. Having taken charge of just six games, Toppmöller is Lens’s shortest-serving manager since the second world war. His exit says more about the club than it does the man. Explaining the parting of ways, the chief executive, Benjamin Parrot, revealed a divide, not necessarily between Toppmöller and his squad, but rather within the staff itself.

“Even before the Trophée des Champions, we felt, within the staff, that there was a French group and then a more international group,” said Parrot. Toppmöller brought two assistants with him. Lens tried to sack one of them, Nelson Morgado, but Toppmöller stayed loyal to his assistant and refused to accept his dismissal. He left and Cahuzac stepped up in his place.

View image in fullscreen Paris Brunner and Denis Zakaria embrace after Monaco take the lead in their win against Lens. Photograph: Alunno Nicolas/Abaca/Shutterstock

Cahuzac was touted as Toppmöller’s successor before he had even settled at the club. That can’t be a healthy environment for any new manager. Perhaps the writing was always on the wall for Toppmöller, especially given that Leca – Cahuzac’s close friend and former teammate at Bastia – is the club’s sporting director. Leca knows how it looks. “Yes, he is my friend, but inside these walls he isn’t my friend. Inside these walls, I am his line manager,” said Leca.

To suggest that Cahuzac’s appointment is pure nepotism is unfair. Lorient were one of the most tactically interesting teams in Ligue 1 last season and while Pantaloni – who was nominated for the manager-of-the-season award – earned most of the plaudits, Cahuzac played a key role too. He also knows the club, having played for them for three seasons and worked under Haise as an assistant.

His first game in charge, against Monaco, did not begin well. The hosts were 1-0 up at half-time but they had the ball in the Lens net on three occasions, denied by the assistant referee’s flag. Cahuzac changed tactics at the interval, which helped, and Matthieu Udol headed in a deserved equaliser. Franjo Ivanovic and Thorgan Hazard had chances as Lens pushed for a winner. In the end, it was a Lens player who scored but, unfortunately for Jonathan Gradit, it was into his own net.

So, Cahuzac’s tenure begins with a valiant 2-1 defeat. The 41-year-old was a pitbull of a player but he was almost inert in his dugout. He stood like a statue, with his hand on his chin in a pensive pose that exuded a studious serenity. After the turbulent week Lens have had, the club need a sense of calm.

Quick Guide Ligue 1 results Show Auxerre 2-1 Brest Nice 2-1 Lille Marseille 1-2 PSG Paris FC 2-1 Strasbourg Angers 2-0 Troyes Le Mans 2-1 Lorient Lyon 4-0 Rennes Toulouse 3-2 Le Havre Monaco 2-1 Lens Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Talking points

On the topic of messy break-ups, there was an unhappy reunion between Liam Rosenior and Strasbourg on Saturday. The pair had not met since Rosenior was hurried out the door to join sister club Chelsea in January. There is no love lost. The Englishman led Paris FC to a 2-1 win, continuing his unbeaten run since returning to Ligue 1 this summer. He celebrated the win in front of the travelling Strasbourg fans, a response, Rosenior said, to insulting chants about his family from the away end. An unsavoury confrontation between both sets of players and staff ensued. Rosenior said the chants had gone “too far” and that “celebrating like that was clearly a message”. His players also sent a message, confirming that they are in the mix for Champions League qualification.

View image in fullscreen Liam Rosenior celebrated Paris FC’s win in front of the travelling Strasbourg fans. Photograph: Matthieu Mirville/Zuma Press Wire/Shutterstock

PSG beat Marseille 2-1 in a Classique that encapsulated the clubs’ seasons so far; both are struggling. For PSG, the points are at least now flowing. Ferran Torres continues to prove a fine signing. He came off the bench to score the opening goal. Marquinhos redeemed himself for his own goal in this fixture last season, which gave Marseille their first win over PSG at the Vélodrome in Ligue 1 in 14 years. That feels like a long time ago now. The concerns for Marseille only deepen. There were bright moments, notably Angel Gomes’s equaliser, but Bruno Génésio’s side have now lost four of their first five league matches. “A Ligue 2 project?” read a banner from the home fans. They go into the international break in the relegation zone.

Despite the game being briefly suspended after the home fans unfurled an insulting banner that targeted their fierce rivals Saint-Étienne, Lyon made a statement with a 4-0 win over Rennes. They rotated in their midweek Europa League win over Anderlecht, a clear but disappointing sign of where their priorities lie. It paid off, however. Rennes fielded a stronger side against Sturm Graz but did not take the three points, and their striker Esteban Lepaul was consequently not involved from the start against Lyon. A full-strength Lyon made short work of Franck Haise’s side, who may struggle to balance their European and league commitments. Rennes did not lay a glove on Lyon, whose own fans posed the greatest threat.

This is an article by Get French Football News

Sports.title: Arsenal, Liverpool and Manchester United told to consider signing ‘wrecking ball’ Premier League star
Sports.content:
Arsenal, Liverpool and Manchester United should think about making a move to sign Sunderland striker Brian Brobbey.

That's according to journalist Darren Lewis, who believes Brobbey could lead the line for the Premier League giants.



4 Premier League giants have been urged to make a move for Brobbey after his hat-trick last weekend Credit: Getty

The Netherlands international scored a superb hat-trick against Manchester City at the Etihad Stadium on Sunday.

They were his first goals of the top-flight campaign, but his game is much more than goals, as the forward uses his strength to brush off defenders and hold up play as a brilliant target man.

And Lewis thinks that quality is exactly what some of the 'Big Six' need, calling on them to potentially bring him in.



Brobbey is 'a one-man wrecking ball'

He said on talkSPORT's Kick-Off with Adrian Durham: “I watched him play in the Netherlands game vs Sweden at the World Cup.

"It was a fantastic example of terrific centre forward play. He was bullying centre-halves, latching onto balls from the wide areas.



“The way that Ronald Koeman played him was superb because he was just a one-man wrecking ball."

Lewis added: "I see him as an option at Liverpool... with his strength, but his vision and his ability to read the game so well.



"And to take advantage, latch onto one centre-half, then another. And just intimidate and frighten the life out of them.

"Man United could really do with somebody with that capability.

"I think Arsenal could [too], absolutely.”

4 Brobbey has been labelled a 'wrecking ball' for his impressive hold-up play and strength Credit: Getty

Would Arsenal, Liverpool or Man United buy Brobbey?

Arsenal only signed Viktor Gyokeres last summer, but he seems to have already lost his starting place to Kai Havertz.

Gyokeres was linked to an exit in August, with Mikel Arteta going on to firmly state that he wouldn't be going anywhere.



However, after his slow start to the season, could the Gunners be tempted to move on and bring in Brobbey instead?

As for Liverpool, Alexander Isak appears to be finding some of his old form, while Hugo Ekitike will return from his injury at the end of this year, so they may not move for a new striker.

For Man United though, they appear to be crying out for a solid No.9, with Benjamin Sesko still struggling to make an impact and Joshua Zirkzee in the same boat.

Matheus Cunha and Bryan Mbuemo have stood in up front, but signing Brobbey could allow them to flourish in their more natural positions and bring something extra to United's attack.



4 Man United have had troubles up front this season - could Brobbey be a solution? Credit: Getty

An 'old-school' striker

talkSPORT's Danny Murphy thinks Brobbey needs to keep scoring goals if he wants to make a move to a Premier League giant.

The 24-year-old has ten goals in 38 Sunderland appearances in all competitions since joining from Ajax for £17million.

Murphy also believes he's 'not aesthetically pleasing' to watch play, but that that's what makes him such a fan favourite.



The ex-Premier League midfielder said: “He's very old school and brilliant at what he does and we all love that because we all remember seeing players very much like him.

“He needs to keep scoring, of course, as a striker because if you're not scoring, the rest of it's irrelevant.

"But he's not aesthetically pleasing to what most football fans or younger football fans are used to.

4 Brobbey has scored 10 goals for Sunderland since joining the club last year Credit: AFP



“The kids who grow up playing FIFA. The skills and the tricks and the flicks. I think that we've moved away a little bit from what's effective and what's good on the football pitch to what we like to see.

"I think the younger generation likes the player that might not score so much... might not hold the ball up all the time, but it's just the way football is.

"I think if I was a player, if I was a midfielder playing with him [I'd love it]. So good!”

Sports.title: Man United could sign wonderkid, 15, who smashed Erling Haaland feat as JJ Gabriel replacement
Sports.content:
Man United could sign wonderkid, 15, who smashed Erling Haaland feat as JJ Gabriel replacement

Manchester United have reportedly been scouting another 15-year-old wonderkid as a potential replacement for JJ Gabriel.

Gabriel travelled to Barcelona last week for transfer talks following the bombshell news that he wanted to leave Man United.



2 Gabriel wants his Man United registration cancelled and has interest from multiple giants - but have the Red Devils spotted a replacement? Credit: Getty

The teenage sensation looked to be on a path to potential stardom at Old Trafford, but he sees his future elsewhere.

Barca and Real Madrid are understood to be the most viable options for Gabriel should he pursue a move abroad.

Meanwhile, Chelsea, Arsenal and Manchester City hold interest in the forward, who has plenty of impressive suitors.



His next move is still undecided, Man United may be beginning a Gabriel contingency plan.

Man United's JJ Gabriel replacement?

Man United are reported to have been tracking 15-year-old Norwegian forward Gabriel Rajkovic.



Rajkovic has already been playing first-team football in his home country with Valerenga, featuring 15 times this season.

He has netted three goals and provided one assist in that time, attracting interest from across the globe.



Reports from Norway also claim that Barcelona have sent scouts to watch him, with Arsenal and Chelsea monitoring too.

Rajkovic doesn't turn 16 until February, and until then, he won't be able to transfer to another club abroad.

As well as that, the left-footed forward is contracted with Valerenga until 2028, so he may be in no rush to take a step up.

2 Rajkovic scored his first Eliteserien goal at a much younger age than Haaland managed Credit: Getty



Rajkovic smashes Haaland feat

Rajkovic has certainly built an impressive reputation in Norway already, having smashed Erling Haaland's feat.

Haaland, who is now arguably the best striker in world football, scored his first goal in the Eliteserien - the Norwegian top flight - aged 17 years and 16 days old.

Meanwhile, Rajkovic netted his first at 15 years, five months, and 15 days old, beating the Manchester City star by a long way.

His maiden strike came in August against Bodo/Glimt, on the same day Barcelona were reportedly scouting him.



He is the Eliteserien's second youngest scorer ever, behind Arsenal's Premier League-winning captain Martin Odegaard.

Odegaard still holds the record, having scored for Stromsgodset in 2014, aged 15 years, four months and 29 days old.

Sports.title: I feared my career was over, but Craig Bellamy inspired me back from the brink
Sports.content:
I feared my career was over, but Craig Bellamy inspired me back from the brink

Wales winger Wes Burns has Craig Bellamy to thank for helping shake fears that his football career was over after an ACL injury.

Burns suffered a serious knee injury in January 2025 and missed 342 days of action, leading to doubts he would ever play again.



5 Burns has opened up about his struggles and Bellamy's vital help when recovering from his ACL injury Credit: Getty

But the 31-year-old managed to fight through a long recovery to return to the pitch for Ipswich at the turn of the year.

And now, having signed for Leicester City in the summer, he has been called up to represent his country under Bellamy.

Burns had missed the last seven Wales camps due to his injury and the tough task of getting back to full fitness again.



However, Bellamy has included him in his squad this month for the Dragons' clashes against Cristiano Ronaldo's Portugal and Erling Haaland's Norway as well as two meetings with Denmark.

It is the first time since October 2024 that the 22-cap man has been called up to a squad for an international break.



Burns thanks Bellamy for 'amazing gesture'

Speaking from the Wales camp, Burns revealed that he is delighted to be back working with manager Bellamy, who had been in regular contact with him over his gruelling recovery period.

"The main thing with the boss here that I enjoy the most is, although I've been away from camp for almost two years now, I've pretty much spoken to him once a month, every other month since I did my ACL," he revealed to talkSPORT's Laurence Mora.



"Which is an amazing gesture from him and a massive plus for me, as he never made me feel like I was too far away from the squad.

"He always made me feel like I was a part of what was being built here, so to come back into his squad is a massive, proud moment for more from where I've been in terms of my injury.

"I can't thank him enough for what he did for me during that time."

5 Burns missed almost an entire year after suffering a serious knee injury for Ipswich against Liverpool in January 2025 Credit: AFP

5 The winger is now back in the Wales squad for the first time since October 2024 Credit: Getty



When asked whether it meant to him that Bellamy was keeping in touch, Burns spoke further on the loneliness of recovery.

"It's weird because it feels like football forgets you... you're grafting in the gym on your own or your physio, you can sort of feel very isolated and that you're not really that footballer anymore, you're just a guy in the gym trying to get fit," he admitted.

"But for him to continually check in on me and give me bits of advice from when he did his knee, times have advanced and things have changed, but just from the mental side of it, it was a massive plus.

"He made sure that I was always doing the right things and kept me in line if I felt like I was deviating... struggling to find the motivation to go into the gym again, he always kept me in line.



"Obviously he didn't have to do that and I think it just goes a long way to show the type of man that he is."

5 Wales boss Bellamy kept in contact with Burns and helped him hugely during his recovery Credit: PA

5 Burns has thanked his international boss for sticking with him during a time when he felt he may never play football again Credit: Getty

Burns admits fears of career being over

A call-up for Wales this month is a huge moment for Burns that has rewarded all of his hard work fighting back from injury.



Bellamy's help clearly made a big impact, particularly as the Leicester forward was going through a time when he didn't know whether he would be able to play football ever again.

He explained: "I think that [not playing again] always crosses your mind when you're going through the rehab and going back to playing football.

"You always question whether you're going to be at the same level when you come back.

"Did it cross my mind that I might not get a chance to come back and play for Wales? Yeah, of course.



"But it also crossed my mind that I might not play football again when I first did my injury.

"So, it's just one of those things. You have to take it in your stride and I'm incredibly grateful to be here again."

Burns will hope to make what will likely be an emotional first appearance for Wales in almost two years when they take on Portugal in the Nations League on Thursday evening.

Sports.title: Club bottom of the EFL has second match postponed one week after first cancellation
Sports.content:
Club bottom of the EFL has second match postponed one week after first cancellation

Crawley Town have announced that their upcoming fixture against Walsall has been postponed due to international call-ups.

The League Two side currently sit bottom of the table after seven games, having lost five times and winning just once so far.

2 Crawley's meeting with Walsall has been postponed due to international call-ups Credit: Getty

They were scheduled to take on Walsall, who are unbeaten and second in the division, on Saturday, October 3.

However, on Monday it was confirmed by the club that the match was going to be moved to a later date.

Crawley call off Walsall fixture

Three of Crawley's players have been called up by their nations to feature during the new, extended international break, which meant they were eligible to request a postponement, as per EFL rules.

The club wrote: "Dion Pereira has been selected to represent Antigua and Barbuda, and Johnny Russell and Nicholas Michalski have been chosen to represent Northern Ireland and England at youth level respectively.

"The club would like to congratulate the trio on being called up to represent their nations on the international stage, and wishes them all success during their time away."

A new date for the clash with Walsall is yet to be confirmed.

Midfielder Pereira has featured four times for Crawley so far this season, scoring once and making one start.

Meanwhile, Russell has played six games in League Two for the Red Devils, starting in their defeat to Grimsby last weekend.

And goalkeeper Michalski has been between the sticks in five of Crawley's opening seven league games.

So, rather than playing without three of their regulars, the club has decided to postpone their fixture instead.

2 Kazim-Richards' side won't have a League Two match until October 10 after having two games called off Credit: Getty

What other League Two games have been postponed?

Crawley, who are managed by former EFL star and Turkey international Colin Kazim-Richards, have now had two upcoming games called off.

Just a week ago, their clash with Barnet was postponed due to international call-ups too.

It now means their next League Two fixture will be on October 10, three weeks after their most recent league match.

Elsewhere in the fourth tier, Port Vale have had games against Northampton and Colchester rescheduled.

Northampton have also seen their game against Oldham moved.

15 League One games have been called off too, including MK Dons vs Bromley, while Reading have opted to keep their clash against Wycombe on, despite having three international call-ups.

Sports.title: Simon Jordan offers advice to Martin O’Neill after ‘strange’ response to Celtic’s Old Firm defeat
Sports.content:
Simon Jordan has urged Martin O'Neill to come back swinging after the Celtic boss cast doubt over his future as manager.

The Scottish champions endured a nightmare seven days as they were beaten by Old Firm rivals Rangers twice in that period.



4 O'Neill has suffered three defeats in the space of seven days Credit: Getty

O'Neill's side lost 1-0 at Celtic Park to end their perfect start to the Scottish Premiership season, which followed a 3-0 defeat in the Scottish League Cup at Ibrox.

To make matters worse, the Hoops also suffered a reverse at home against Hungarian side Ferencvaros in the Europa League on Thursday night.

Celtic have now lost four matches in all competitions this season, as many as they did in 35 games under O'Neill last term.



The 74-year-old was handed a one-year deal in June after guiding Celtic to a league and Scottish Cup double during his return for a second spell as caretaker manager in January.

O'Neill's bleak assessment

Following Celtic's latest Old Firm defeat, O'Neill cast doubt over his future in the role and admitted he was considering whether he was the right man to lead the team.



He told reporters: "I genuinely will reflect and see.

"It's a matter of whether I can help the team. If that's the case - the manager’s supposed to be able to do that. I will have a look at that there this week.

"I think that every single time that something crops up things don't go so well, age plays a part, and you know what? They may well be right - you know I'm 110 in two years time.



“So yeah, it might be time to wrap it up.”

Jordan tells O'Neill to fight back

Following O'Neill's comments on his future, talkSPORT's Jordan has insisted the Northern Irishman should have delivered a more defiant message in the wake of a difficult run of results.

4 Ryan Naderi scored the only goal as Rangers beat Celtic for the second week in a row Credit: Getty

He said on White and Jordan: “I've liked to see him being a bit spikier and a bit more robust, rather than sounding relatively defeated in that clip.

Explaining how he would have reacted, the ex-Crystal Palace chairman said: “I certainly would have been wanting to say back to them, ‘This has happened, it will not happen again - I have to accept the fact this week, put aside the European game which I'm disappointed in as well, but losing twice to Rangers in a week does not happen at this football club I have to take responsibility for and it's not happening again’.



“I would have liked to have heard that."

With O'Neill previously a regular on talkSPORT's White and Jordan show, Jordan admitted the press conference came as a shock to him.

Highlighting Celtic's reverse defeat in Sunday's Old Firm - where away fans weren't allowed at Celtic Park - the talkSPORT host claimed he will likely have been hurting.

Jordan continued: “The fact that he's talking about whether he can help the team and whether it's his time - I find that slightly strange of Martin, but he's having a reflective moment.

4 O'Neill has admitted he is considering his future as Celtic manager Credit: Getty



“He's not enjoyed the discreditation of his side, because he did turn around and say during the course of last week, ‘We'll see how they get on when they come back to a place where they haven't got their fans to support them’.

“So he won't like that, he needs to get his shoulders back and his chest out."

'Tough get going'

O'Neill previously spent five years in charge of Celtic between 2000 and 2005, during which time he won seven trophies including three league titles and reached a UEFA Cup final.

And Jordan urged O'Neill to remember his past achievements as he called on him to portray a more confident exterior going forward.



He added: “He's still the same man.

"There's nothing that happened in Martin's life physically or mentally to change the difference between the guy that came in and got them centred on being a decent Celtic side to win the Scottish Premiership whatever that's worth to us English [people] that watch a proper league.

4 O'Neill won two trophies with Celtic in the 2025/26 season Credit: Getty

“But he needs to regain that poise, because he's Martin O'Neill and he's better than the results as they stand at this moment in time, and he's better than that interview.”

Rounding off, Jordan urged O'Neill to stand firm in the face of adversity, insisting he accepted the challenges of his role when he took on the permanent role at Celtic Park.



Jordan said: “He took the job knowing what the challenges were and he went into another season wanting to embrace it and he danced around playing a little quizzical Irishman with the media, and about how old he was and stuff.

“But he took the job on, and now it's tough. And when it gets tough, get going.”

Sports.title: Jason Cundy: I was bullied when I played for Tottenham, it was a disgrace
Sports.content:
Jason Cundy: I was bullied when I played for Tottenham, it was a disgrace

Tottenham's medical staff won't be receiving Christmas cards from Jason Cundy any time soon.

Cundy, who began his career at Chelsea, was on the books at Spurs from 1992 until 1996 but managed only 28 appearances for the club.



1 Cundy signed for Chelsea as a 17-year-old and went on to make 53 appearances Credit: Getty

That's because his stint in north London was blighted by injuries.

Annoyingly for the beloved Sports Bar co-host, a number of his physical struggles were manageable.

Jason Cundy rips into Tottenham's medical team

"Spurs, their medical team were nothing short of abysmal. They were terrible," Cundy said on In The Mixer.

"And part of my injuries that lasted for as long as they did was partly down to their incompetence. They were a disgrace."



One example of Spurs' medical staff mishandling Cundy was when he got diagnosed with a bulging disc, which sat in his nerve canal.

"I had scoliosis, it's a curvature of the spine," Cundy said.

"That can be remedied or rectified by exercise, hard work, physio."

Cundy detailed that injured players at Spurs during his time at the club went in earlier during the week to receive treatment.



How Spurs' medics bullied Jason Cundy

But once it reached the end of the week, Cundy couldn't take any more.

"By the Friday, I'm like, 'I'm not going in,'" Cundy said.

"So I phoned the PFA and said they're (Spurs) bullying me to try and get an operation."



The PFA, who Cundy hailed as 'absolutely magnificent', then organised for the defender to see a physio on Harley Street, which is recognised as an distinguished medical district in central London.

"And the physios at Spurs basically washed their hands of me, didn't want to know me," Cundy added.

"And within six weeks of seeing a physio at Harley Street, I was back training.

"I'd been out close to two years."

Cundy was eventually forced to retire in 2000 aged just 31 due to injuries, with a training ground incident while at Portsmouth proving to be the straw that broke the camel's back.

Sports.title: Arsenal star left out of squad for national team after just one start this season
Sports.content:
Arsenal star left out of squad for national team after just one start this season

New Ecuador head coach Marcelo Gallardo has not selected Arsenal star Piero Hincapie for his first squad.

Ecuador take on South Korea in a friendly, as well as Japan and one of Panama or New Zealand in a four-team tournament during the extended international break.

2 Hincapie has struggled for regular game time under Mikel Arteta this season

However, they'll do so without the Gunners defender, which is a boost for Mikel Arteta's men.

The former Bayer Leverkusen man has started just once in all competitions for the 2025/26 Premier League champions, that coming in the 1-0 win over Napoli in the Champions League.

The 24-year-old missed subsequent wins over Sunderland and Ipswich due to an injury sustained in training after the Napoli victory.

And while Hincapie, whose loan move was made permanent over the summer, returned to the matchday squad for the 3-0 defeat at Brighton and Hove Albion on Saturday, the Ecuadorian was an unused sub at the Amex Stadium.

It does mean that Hincapie has extra time to build up fitness ahead of the game against Leeds next month.

Hincapie, though, is currently suspended for the South American side in competitive matches owing to his dismissal in the round-of-32 defeat to Mexico at the 2026 World Cup.

The player would be eligible for the game against South Korea but Gallardo turned his attention elsewhere as he looks to make a winning start to life as Ecuador boss.

Caicedo also missing

Hincapie isn't the only Premier League star to have been overlooked for Gallardo's first squad.

Moises Caicedo has also missed out on an international call-up, which will suit Chelsea.

2 Caicedo has also been overlooked for Ecuador Credit: AFP

The midfielder has featured just once since the 2026 World Cup, and that was a 14-minute cameo in the 4-3 over Brighton last month.

Caicedo hasn't made an appearance since he was forced off in the second-half of the seven-goal thriller.

Sunderland pair Nilson Angulo and Juan Riquelme Angulo have both been selected by Caicedo for their Asian tour.

Middlesbrough's Jeremy Sarmiento has also made the cut for La Tri.

Other household names have also been selected by Gallardo, including Paris Saint-Germain's Willian Pacho and former Brighton left-back Pervis Estupinan, who now plies his trade at AC Milan.

Sports.title: Cole Palmer’s commitment to England questioned as Chelsea star urged to make statement
Sports.content:
Cole Palmer's England commitment has been challenged by talkSPORT stalwart Adrian Durham.

The Chelsea star was called up by Three Lions boss Thomas Tuchel for upcoming UEFA Nations League games against Spain, Czechia and Croatia, which are live on talkSPORT.

3 Palmer deserved his England recall but he's one of five players to withdraw from Tuchel's squad Credit: Getty

It marked the first time Tuchel had turned to the former Manchester City man since his 2026 World Cup snub.

However, the 24-year-old has since withdrawn from the national team set-up despite playing the full 90 minutes in Friday's 3-0 defeat at Brentford.

Palmer is one of several who have pulled out of the squad, with Declan Rice, Tino Livramento, Kobbie Mainoo and Marcus Rashford all returning to the parent sides 'due to respective injury issues'.

Morgan Gibbs-White and James Garner have since been drafted into the England squad for the upcoming Nations League clashes.

'He was awful'

Durham, though, wasn't happy about Palmer's decision to return to his parent side, voicing his displeasure on Hawksbee & Jacobs on Monday afternoon.

"I am starting to question Cole Palmer's commitment to England," Durham began as Palmer was discussed.

"14 caps, two goals. He's played in one World Cup qualifier in his career, and in that he was awful away to Andorra [in June 2025]."

Durham continued: "He's played five times for England since the Euros when he scored in the final. England have had 28 games since the Euro final in 2024 [vs Spain]."

Palmer failed to make Tuchel's England squad in North America over the summer, and was one of a number of high-profile players, including Phil Foden and Harry Maguire, that were overlooked.

3 Tuchel snubbed Palmer for a England call-up for the 2026 World Cup Credit: Getty

"I can accept if a player is not fully fit, I get that," Durham added. "And if this is the case, that he has an injury that's ruling him out, then fine, I totally get it.

"I've got a lot of sympathy with injured players. But let me give you that stat again. He's played in five England games since the Euro final. And that's five out of 28."

Durham questions Palmer's England desire

Durham then demanded answers from Palmer, asking if he even wanted to play for England.

"I'm questioning his commitment to England," Durham said. "Does he really want to play for England? If you don't, tell the world you don't want to play for England.

"Because just picking and choosing when you want to play for England is actually disrupting other number 10s like [Nottingham Forest's] Morgan Gibbs-White, like [Fulham's] Josh King, who might want to play for England.

3 Durham has called Palmer's England commitment into question following his withdrawal Credit: Getty

"We're all agreed Cole Palmer is a really good footballer. But, other than that goal in the Euro final, I've not really seen, on a consistent basis, any kind of quality or commitment from him.

"So let's have it from Cole Palmer. Do you want to play for England or do you not want to play for England?"

'Do one'

Meanwhile, talkSPORT presenter Jamie O'Hara believes that Palmer should tell the Chelsea medical staff to 'do one' and represent his nation anyway.

Speaking on Breakfast on Monday morning, the former Tottenham Hotspur midfielder said: "I've had medical staff try to turn around to me and say, 'No, you should only play 60 minutes.

"How about no? How about, 'I'm in charge of my own destiny? I'm in charge of my football career. You ain't in charge of my football career, I am.'

"Then Cole Palmer has to be a man and say, 'No, I've been out, I've missed out on the England squad. I've missed a World Cup last season because I was injured and I weren't playing, and I come back and I weren't fit.'

"'Now I am fit, and I'm ready to go and Thomas Tuchel called me up, I'm going, and if you say I'm not going, I'm still going. I'm getting in my car and I'm driving there to St George's Park because I want to be involved with England.

"'And you can't tell me some geezer who's in charge of load management can tell me that I ain't going to play for my country.'

"Do one."

Sports.title: Gary Lineker labels Sir Jim Ratcliffe an 'unpleasant human being' in scathing attack on Man United co-owner - and congratulates the Glazers on 'finding someone even worse than them'
Sports.content:
Gary Lineker has delivered a scathing verdict on Sir Jim Ratcliffe's running of Manchester United, branding the club's co-owner an 'unpleasant human being'.

There was optimism when the 73-year-old bought a minority stake in the historic club in February 2024 and took control of football operations.

That mood now appears to have soured among sections of the fanbase, however, amid poor results on the pitch and growing frustration with decisions made under Ratcliffe's leadership.

Speaking on The Rest is Football podcast, England legend Lineker said: 'I look at Man United and I see problems coming down from the top.

'I must congratulate the Glazers on finding someone even worse than them that they can blame and getting him in there and getting all the stick: Jim Ratcliffe.

'I don’t think he’s a particularly pleasant human being and it’s a bit of a shambles of a football club the way it’s being run at the moment. So, well done to the Glazers on that one, deflecting everything away from them!'

'I must congratulate the Glazers on finding someone even worse than them that they can blame and getting him in there and getting all the stick: Jim Ratcliffe,' Lineker said

United fans protested against the club's ownership ahead of and during the Man City derby

United have already parted company with two permanent managers since Ratcliffe took charge of football operations. Erik ten Hag was sacked three months after being handed a new deal in October 2024, while his replacement, Ruben Amorim, departed in January this year after 14 months in charge.

Michael Carrick was appointed permanent manager in the summer after impressing in an interim role, recording 11 wins and three draws from 16 matches to steer the club back into the Champions League, but an underwhelming transfer window followed.

United missed out on targets Elliot Anderson and Matheus Fernandes, while they head into the international break in 12th place with just five points from their opening five games of the season.

In the last week academy starlet JJ Gabriel, nicknamed 'Kid Messi', has requested to leave the club due to his family's view that it has fallen behind the heavyweights of European football.

Daily Mail Sport has reported that a source close to the family explained that United are 'far away' from the likes of Barcelona, Real Madrid, Bayern Munich as well as domestic rivals Arsenal and Manchester City, and that they want him to 'learn from the best' to maximise his talents.

Away from the pitch, Ratcliffe has been much-maligned for mass staff redundancies as well as increasing match ticket prices and season-ticket relocations in order to accommodate further hospitality seating. Ratcliffe also plans to build a new 100,000-seater stadium.

Fans protested against United's ownership ahead of and during September's Manchester derby defeat, and supporters' groups have called on Ratcliffe to resign over his recent comments on immigration.

Lineker added: 'It is a bit of a mess, that club. You've got a ground that's falling apart, all sorts of complaints about various things.

Talented youngster JJ Gabriel, nicknamed 'Kid Messi', has requested to leave the club due to his family's view that it has fallen behind the heavyweights of European football

'They're losing young teenagers, it looks like that (Gabriel leaving) is going to happen.

'The results, the inconsistency seems to be back. They have backed the manager many times and it’s not worked for them but there’s got to be something dripping down from the top.'

Previously, Ratcliffe has said that excessive criticism would cause him to walk away from the club if he was 'abused' by fans in the same way the Glazer family have.

The unpopular Glazer family bought the club in 2005 via a leveraged takeover and retain a majority stake.

'I mean, I can put up with it for a while,' Ratcliffe said in March. 'I don't mind being unpopular because I get that nobody likes seeing Manchester United down where they are, and nobody likes the decisions we're having to make at the moment.

'If I draw a bit of the ire, I can put up with that. But I'm no different to the average person. It's not nice, particularly for friends and family.

'So, eventually, if it reached the extent that the Glazer family have been abused, then I'd have to say, look, enough's enough guys, let somebody else do this.

'They can't really come to a match, the Glazers. They've retreated into the shadows a bit now, so I'm getting all the stick.'

Sports.title: Tottenham plunged deeper into the mire as relegation chances soar, while Arsenal and Man City pull clear in two-horse title race: Supercomputer's updated Premier League predictions after five games
Sports.content:
Tottenham plunged deeper into the mire as relegation chances soar, while Arsenal and Man City pull clear in two-horse title race: Supercomputer's updated Premier League predictions after five games

The international break is here, giving Premier League clubs time to take stock of what has been a thrilling start to the 2026-27 season, and Opta to reevaluate their title predictions for the season's close.

We're only five games in and there are already a number of intriguing storylines developing, not least so-called relegation favourites Hull City's rampant return to the top flight after nine years away, claiming eight points to sit eighth heading into the break.

Enzo Maresca's start to life in charge of Manchester City couldn't have gone any better, winning all five games to clinch top spot as the only team with a 100 per cent record.

Brighton's stunning 3-0 defeat of Arsenal at the weekend has left the Premier League champions in second, while Fabian Hurzeler's side are next in line in third.

Only goal difference separates fourth to seventh in Brentford, Leeds, Liverpool and Everton, who each remain unbeaten so far.

Meanwhile, Chelsea are 10th with seven points, Michael Carrick's Manchester United are 12th and Tottenham, despite spending around £302million this summer, sit bottom of the table after collecting just two points. With Opta now giving them a 30 per cent chance of relegation, the outlook is already looking bleak for Roberto De Zerbi's side.

City's chances to win the title have increased considerably, closing the gap on Arsenal to 39.8 per cent, with Opta essentially predicting a two-horse race

To recap, Opta's supercomputer gave Arsenal a 40.6 per cent chance of retaining their title at the start of the campaign, making them favourites.

Manchester City were comfortably second favourites at 19.6 per cent, followed by Liverpool with 9.2 per cent and Manchester United with 6.6 per cent.

Interestingly, despite suffering that heavy defeat to the Seagulls at the weekend, Arsenal remain Opta's favourites to lift the trophy at the end of the season, with that percentage increasing to 43.7 per cent.

At the same time, City's chances have also increased considerably, closing the gap on Arsenal to 39.8 per cent, with Opta essentially predicting a two-horse race.

Liverpool are third favourites, but only with 5.7 per cent, that figure dropping slightly from the start of the season.

Brighton are now fourth favourites with 4.2 per cent. Brentford are fifth (1.2 per cent), Everton sixth (1.1 per cent) and Chelsea seventh (1.0 per cent).

Man United have struggled to put points on the board so far despite leading the Premier League for total shots (113) and touches in the opposition box (182). They have, as a result, fallen from fourth favourites at the beginning of the season to eighth, having just a 0.9 per cent chance of winning the title, the biggest fall of any team.

Aston Villa picked up their first win of the season against rock-bottom Spurs but lost three of their opening four matches and have been given just a 0.7 per cent chance of winning the title.

Join the discussion Should Spurs fans be furious about their club’s dramatic decline despite massive transfer spending?

Opta are giving Spurs a 30 per cent chance of relegation after their poor start to the season

And despite getting off to a strong start, Xabi Alonso's Chelsea side have now gone three games without a win and are given a 0.95 per cent chance of winning the title.

At the other end of the table, Coventry City, despite winning their first game of the season against Nottingham Forest at the weekend, are favourites to go down, with Opta giving them a 45.1 per cent chance of relegation.

Next in line for the drop are Alvaro Arbeloa's Fulham, who have a 42.4 per cent chance of relegation.

And finally, Roberto De Zerbi's Tottenham are third favourites to fall into the Championship at the end of the season, with the supercomputer having given them a 30 per cent chance of relegation.

Sports.title: Paul Merson questions Mikel Arteta's decision to start £75m ace Bruno Guimaraes ahead of Myles Lewis-Skelly in Brighton rout
Sports.content:
Paul Merson believes Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta made a mistake in starting Bruno Guimaraes against Brighton.

The Brazilian midfielder struggled – along with the rest of his team-mates – as the Gunners were soundly beaten 3-0 on the south coast.

'I’d like to ask Mikel Arteta what his thinking was behind playing Bruno Guimaraes over Myles Lewis-Skelly,' wrote former Arsenal forward Merson in his Sky Sports column.

'I don’t know if he thought it would be a nice football match, that Brighton would be tired after coming from 2-0 down against Manchester United on Wednesday?

'It just didn’t work. Arsenal got outrun, they got overpowered in midfield, they got ripped to shreds.

'Bruno’s a good footballer. If you’re playing a low block, I don’t see the problem in playing him. When you’re going to dominate the ball, there’s no-one like him when you have time. He’s a good player and passer – and he’s very intelligent.

Guimaraes struggled – along with the rest of his team-mates – as the Gunners were soundly beaten 3-0 on the south coast

'I just wonder if Arteta was sitting on the coach on the way back thinking "I’ve got that one wrong".

'When Bruno came on as a sub against Aston Villa a few weeks ago, he was outstanding. He could just keep the ball, pop it around, play one-twos and play the game at his tempo. That would have been a better idea.

'I’m not blaming Bruno for Arsenal losing, absolutely not. I just didn’t know why Arteta had to change the team in a very difficult game.'

Saturday's defeat left the defending champions second in the table after Manchester City followed up by beating Sunderland on Sunday to clinch the top spot with a three-point margin.

Sports.title: Mo Salah handed six-month driving ban for speeding in his Rolls-Royce - just days after revealing his emotional Liverpool departure
Sports.content:
Mo Salah handed six-month driving ban for speeding in his Rolls-Royce - just days after revealing his emotional Liverpool departure

Former Liverpool footballer Mohamed Salah has been banned from driving for six months after his Rolls-Royce was clocked speeding.

The player failed to tell police who was at the wheel when the car was caught by a speed camera driving at 36mph on a 30mph stretch of road in Wilmslow, Cheshire, on March 27, according to court documents.

The 34-year-old did not respond to the notice of the prosecution, brought by Cheshire Constabulary, and did not enter a plea to the charge.

A court official said he was prosecuted at Warrington Combined Court under the Single Justice Procedure, which sees magistrates sit in private hearings, and was convicted of failing to give information relating to the identification of the driver of the Rolls Royce.

Salah has been banned from driving for six months after his Rolls-Royce was clocked speeding

The Egypt national captain was handed a six-month driving ban and ordered to pay £1,044, the court spokeswoman said.

The speeding offence came days after Salah announced he would be leaving Liverpool following nine years with the team.

Announcing his departure on March 24, the club said he had 'firmly established himself as one of the greatest players in Liverpool’s history'.

He scored 257 goals in 442 appearances for Liverpool, before transferring to Turkish side Trabzonspor following the 2025-26 season.

Sports.title: 'I thought my ankle was going to snap': Andros Townsend speaks for first time on 'terrifying' moment he was RUN OVER by a pitch rolling machine at half-time in Thailand
Sports.content:
Ex-Premier League star Andros Townsend has admitted he was extremely fortunate to escape unscathed after being run over by a pitch roller in Thailand. The former England international, who joined Thai Premier League outfit PT Prachuap during the summer transfer window, looked to have suffered a freak injury when a manned pitch roller ploughed into him as he warmed up at half-time against Pattani. Footage of the incident quickly went viral on social media, but Townsend later made light of the ordeal on his Instagram story, posting: 'It turns out Stoke away wasn't so bad after all. Swipe to see why.' Remarkably, the former Crystal Palace winger was able to walk away from the incident unharmed and even came on as a second-half substitute. Appearing on Piers Morgan's Football Uncensored on Monday night, Townsend admitted it was a 'terrifying' experience but is very grateful to have escaped with only a few 'bumps and bruises'. 'I didn't see it coming,' he said. 'It was at halftime, we were going out to warm up. I saw two rollers on either side of the pitch. 🚨Andros Townsend got lucky to avoid injury during warmups in the Thai League pic.twitter.com/ctEOycMZcF — Polymarket Sports (@PolymarketSport) September 19, 2026 Former Premier League winger Andros Townsend has admitted he was extremely fortunate to escape unscathed after being run over by a pitch roller in Thailand on Saturday 'I remember thinking to myself, "I've never seen that before in my career, what are they doing?" But we got called to warm up. Didn't think anything of it. 'The next I saw him was when I was literally underneath him and thankfully no serious damage. A couple of bumps and bruises but managed to walk away unscathed, luckily. 'Every time I see it, I'm cringing, I'm in disbelief. When I sent it to my kids, my kids thought it was AI. Literally, I had to explain to them, for the next ten minutes, that it was real. 'It's horrible to watch back and to see what could have been but, like I said, thankfully I was fortunate I did manage to fall onto the floor at the right time, so nothing snapped as the roller went over me. And I'm here today to laugh about and tell the story.' As host Morgan pointed out, Townsend's team-mates reacted in horror as the roller mowed him down, fearing the worst for the former Premier League man. Footage showed the driver of the roller struggling to control the vehicle, with Townsend kicking a ball away, not looking in that direction. 'They (my team-mates) were very surprised that I continued the warm up! They were telling me to go to the doctor. They were calling for the stretcher. But listen, I've been around the block, I've had my setbacks, I've had my injury issues. A roller is definitely not going to stop me from continuing, that's for sure, so I was able to carry on. 'It was quite heavy, but I was able to kind of lift [it], force it off me. So when it was completely on me, I was getting crushed a little bit. 'But I was able to push it up, as you can see, as it falls on me, I was able to get my left arm up and relieve some of the pressure… and then I was able to get my team-mates around me who were able to lift it, and I was able to squeeze out but at that moment where it was crushing my left leg, it was quite terrifying, I must say. Townsend was bizarrely run over while warming up for a game at this new club in Thailand 'I was thinking I was done because it was my ankle, which I've had operated on. It was up my left knee, which I've had operated on. So I thought, either my left ankle was going to snap or my left knee is going to snap. I thought I was done. I was very fortunate that I was able to hobble away and recover within a few minutes.' PT Prachuap - based in Prachuap Khiri Khan province, 150 miles south of Bangkok - appeared to have leaked Townsend's arrival two weeks before he joined when they asked if anyone had a three-bedroom house available for the player to live in. They are the 17th club of his career. Townsend made 29 appearances for Kanchanaburi Power last season, scoring three goals. He has previously played for Spurs, Newcastle, Palace and Everton, and moved to Thailand after a short spell with Turkish side Antalyaspor. Townsend making the move comes after he worked for ITV as a co-commentator during the World Cup. The ex-England winger went viral at the tournament for his unconventional diet - which includes eating raw steak. He released a slew of videos promoting his all-natural diet including steak, sardines and boiled eggs.
