Sports.title: Lorenzo “Truck” Simpson Wins WBA Intercontinental Light Heavyweight Title
Sports.content:
On Saturday night, September 19th, in the co-main event of the Skyy Myles Promotions event entitled ‘The Supper,’ Lorenzo “Truck” Simpson defeated Shawn McCalman (17-3, 8 KOs) and won the WBA Intercontinental Title.

Going into the fight, the matchup was considered to be a 50/50 bout between two hungry boxers. Winning the vacant title was important to both boxers because it’s a regional belt that provides a boost in the rankings.

In the opening round of the southpaw vs. southpaw bout, McCalman got off to a good start as he was changing levels with an active jab. Simpson put his jab on display in the second round as he landed multiple jabs to the body.

The third round saw Simpson have success in regards to closing the distance and landing the left hand. As the round was coming to a close, McCalman connected with a few body shots.

The fourth round was highlighted by a solid uppercut landed by Simpson. In the fifth round, McCalman upped his production as he got back to working the jab and targeting the body.

The majority of the second half of the bout was fought in close quarters, as the back-and-forth match went the distance.

At the conclusion of the fight, the judges had to determine if they were swayed by McCalman’s volume or Simpson’s sharp power shots.

In a very technical fight, one judge scored the bout (96-94) in favor of Shawn McCalman. However, that judge’s scorecard was overruled by the other two judges, who both scored the fight (97-93) in favor of Lorenzo Simpson.

With the victory, Lorenzo “Truck” Simpson (17-3, 10 KOs) has won a title belt, and now he feels the sky is the limit. Next on his agenda is a bout against a boxer in the top 15.

Back in January 2017, Coach Calvin Ford and Coach Kenny Ellis were in the corner when Gervonta “Tank” Davis won his first world title. Now the question is, will Lorenzo “Truck” Simpson be the next world champion to come out of the Upton Boxing Center?

Sports.title: Keith Connolly Pitches Benn-Eubank Rubber Match at 168
Sports.content:
Conor Benn choosing to leap straight from a second-round knockout loss to Ryan into a third clash against Chris Eubank Jr. at 168 pounds looks like a cash grab rather than a legitimate sporting return. Rushing into another stadium payday before the UK rivalry expires takes precedence over sensible career preservation.

The condition of Benn’s chin demands serious scrutiny after Ryan stunned him inside three minutes and finished the job at 1:25 of round two. Throwing Benn back in the ring against an established, bigger operator after a brief break represents hazardous management. Benn already absorbed punishing artillery over twenty-four rounds during their initial two bouts.

“One hundred percent. 168 pounds, no excuses. The trilogy, another stadium fight, it’ll sell out. It’ll be a tremendous event, and then there’ll be no excuses. There’ll be a winner of the one-one series between the two guys. I expect it to happen. I think it’ll make the event big. Eddie Hearn with Chris Eubank. Myself and Dana White on one side backing Conor,” said manager Keith Connolly to talkSPORT Boxing.

That soundbite benefits Eubank far more than it helps Benn. Eubank escapes the brutal boils down to lower limits and enters the ring fully fueled. Benn piling on weight up to 178.4 pounds on fight night against Ryan merely demonstrated quick fluid retention, not the ability to trade functional super middleweight muscle against a seasoned campaigner.

Carrying sluggish pounds strips away Benn’s hand speed, the single attribute that gave the older man problems. Eubank gains total freedom to march forward, walk through incoming fire, and punish Benn in the pocket without the sapping weight restrictions that limited his output in the past.

The promotional split presents an aggressive battle behind the scenes. Connolly and Dana White would back Benn, with Eddie Hearn positioned in Eubank’s corner. Hearn spent years guiding Benn’s career. Hearn knows his former fighter’s technical deficiencies, stamina thresholds, and gym habits better than anyone else in the sport.

A standard recovery program would keep Benn out of heavy sparring, followed by a controlled confidence builder. Fast-tracking the trilogy brings immense gate receipts while Benn’s marketability remains intact. His management clearly prefers mining this family feud for quick millions rather than risking him against dangerous welterweights.

Eubank secures every physical edge at 168 pounds. Benn assumes all the medical hazards, trading his future punch resistance for one last massive stadium check.

Without Riyadh Season writing blank checks, the math completely falls apart. The first two encounters only happened because Saudi money absorbed the astronomical purses, underwriting the inflated demands of both camps while keeping pay-per-view prices low. Traditional broadcast economics cannot support those figures. If the Saudis decide they have zero interest in funding a third run between two damaged fighters, no standard commercial outfit can bridge the financial void.

DAZN, Boxxer, or Sky Sports operating on standard balance sheets cannot cut ten-million-dollar checks to men coming off definitive stoppage losses. Staging a stadium event at Wembley or Tottenham Hotspur Stadium costs millions just to open the turnstiles and turn on the lights. Gate receipts and a standard UK pay-per-view split would force both men to take a massive haircut from their previous paydays. When reality hits the accountants, the money will dry up fast.

Calling it a celebrity match between nepo babies accurately identifies the true product. Stripped of elite competitive relevance, this pairing relies solely on the nostalgia of their fathers’ names. Ryan exposed Benn inside four minutes as an undersized, one-dimensional slugger with a fragile chin. Eubank has drifted for years without winning a legitimate world title, relying on domestic drama rather than championship credentials.

Neither fighter commands global pay-per-view numbers outside the British market. Without international interest, the fight turns into a regional cash grab. If Dana White and Zuffa step in to foot the bill, they will quickly discover that UK nostalgia does not move subscription needles in North America. When the Saudi money train bypasses the station, both fighters will either take a fraction of their past purses or realize their lucrative family drama has priced itself out of the market.

Sports.title: Shakur Stevenson Makes Zuffa Signing Look Worse
Sports.content:
Zuffa believed it landed pure royalty by securing Shakur Stevenson following his victory against Teofimo Lopez. The subsequent months delivered zero ring appearances, endless social media bickering, alongside an obstinate champion insisting on tailor-made parameters before stepping into the ring.

A lack of signed contracts triggered sharp public reaction.

“Zuffa have to really regret that Shakur Stevenson signing. All he has done is ruin his goodwill with the fans online and continue to be a pain in the ass to get a fight done for,” Tolboof posted on X.

The critique holds immense weight given the presence of ready internal rivals. José Valenzuela threw down an explicit challenge, handing the promotion an explosive pairing of roster talent. Stevenson discarded the possibility entirely.

Rayo delivers relentless offense, legitimate stopping power, plus an eagerness to trade in the pocket. Such an opponent forces Stevenson out of his safety zones, giving the promotional hierarchy a genuine look at their prize asset under fire. Ernesto Mercado offers another devastating threat capable of delivering the carnage Turki Alalshikh expects from these venture millions.

Stevenson ignores those dangerous tests. He spent valuable calendar time chasing Devin Haney at a catchweight limit of 144 pounds, demanding artificial terms against a larger rival. Haney relies on safety-first positioning, backfoot movement, minimal inside engagement. The brass faced grueling backroom wrangling merely to stage a bloodless fencing match devoid of crowd drama.

A collaborative company asset jumps at the Rayo encounter, establishing a fierce homegrown rivalry under the promotional banner. Stevenson prioritized stagnation, fixating on comfortable terms instead of stepping through the ropes.

Pure technical craft is obvious. The actual headache centers on functional execution for the brand. The Riyadh connection thrives on reckless courage, volatility, combatants chasing knockouts against devastating hitters. Stevenson brings retreat-first tactics, endless contract stalling, vast stretches of inactivity.

The brass presented him as their crown jewel. Stevenson spent his entire tenure turning that blockbuster signing into an overpriced promotional nightmare.

Dana White has to be feeling serious buyer’s remorse, even if he will never admit it publicly. White built his entire empire on a matchmaking philosophy that is the exact polar opposite of how Shakur Stevenson operates. In the UFC model, fighters take the hardest fights presented, stay active, and entertain the crowd. Stevenson brings the complete antithesis: high financial demands, a fence-and-retreat style that empties arenas, and an obsession with handpicking circumstances down to the exact pound.

Zuffa shelled out eight figures to make Stevenson a headline acquisition, expecting him to anchor major events. Instead, the promotion bought into months of dead air, endless social media bickering, and outright refusal to engage in in-house tests. Turning down José “Rayo” Valenzuela right out of the gate showed where Stevenson’s priorities sit. Rayo is a dangerous, aggressive hitter within the same organizational family who would have forced a firefight and given the fans real drama. Passing on that test while chasing a 144-pound handicap against Devin Haney proves Stevenson wants the safety of selective terms rather than testing himself against true offensive threats.

That calculated businessman approach is poison for a fledgling promotional brand trying to build genuine momentum. Matchmaking a risk-averse defensive specialist is difficult enough; matchmaking one who demands king’s ransom money while rejecting live punchers is an outright headache. When an elite technician refuses to take risks in the ring or at the negotiating table, the company is left paying millions just to watch its marquee investment gather dust on the shelf.

Triggering an escape clause in the contract would be the quickest way to end the bleeding, because keeping Shakur on the roster is a recipe for stagnation. If the Zuffa brass has a legal mechanism based on turned-down fight offers, inactivity periods, or failure to accept assigned dates, pulling that trigger makes absolute business sense.

The problem with holding onto a fighter like Shakur is the opportunity cost. Every month wasted trying to indulge his catchweight demands against Devin Haney is calendar space denied to fighters who actually want to scrap. Dana White built his promotional legacy by freezing out athletes who attempt to play matchmaker from their couches. In boxing, promoters constantly get trapped paying massive retainers to elite technicians who believe they are entitled to dictate every single term while taking zero operational risk.

Passing publicly on José Valenzuela was the ultimate signal. When an athlete tells his own paymasters that he refuses an in-house clash with a dangerous puncher, he ceases to be a promotional asset and becomes an obstacle. If Zuffa cannot use him to test their own talent or build compelling company events, they are simply subsidizing an ego trip.

Cutting ties via a contractual exit would send a message to the rest of the roster that the money requires reciprocal cooperation. If Shakur wants to wait around for perfect conditions at his leisure, he can do it as a free agent on somebody else’s dime.

Sports.title: Ryan Garcia vs. Teofimo Lopez Talks Target February 6
Sports.content:
Ryan Garcia faces a choice between taking a December date with Isaac Cruz or holding out for a clash with Teofimo Lopez. The second route is complicated by Lopez’s mandatory WBA obligation involving Jack Catterall.

Cruz called for Ryan after stopping Nestor Bravo in six rounds Saturday night in San Diego. Ryan quickly accepted and indicated that an offer would follow.

Preliminary discussions have taken place between representatives for Ryan and Lopez. Chris Mannix revealed that talks have targeted February 6, 2027, at Madison Square Garden.

“There have been conversations between the representatives of Garcia and Lopez about making a Garcia versus Lopez fight, to the point where the conversations even got to a spot where they talked about a date, which is early February. I think February 6th is the date that I was told, and the location is Madison Square Garden in New York City,” said Mannix on his channel.

Mannix prefers Ryan to skip Cruz and go directly into the Teofimo bout. That route assumes the WBA will permit Lopez to bypass Catterall, who defeated Shakhram Giyasov to secure his mandatory claim.

Matchroom has sent formal legal letters urging the sanctioning body to enforce its ruling. Eddie Hearn argues that Catterall’s status carried over with the belt from Rolando Romero to Teofimo. Team Lopez claims the directive applied strictly to Romero and no longer binds the new titleholder.

Mannix’s February target ignores the governing body timeline. Unless Ryan meets Teofimo prior to Catterall’s cited November window, Teofimo must satisfy that mandatory defense. Negotiations, a potential purse bid, a full camp, and physical recovery would make February 6 impractical.

Catterall also represents a stylistic danger for Teofimo. The British southpaw controls distance with a disciplined jab, employs lateral movement and scores with counters without retreating into a shell. He has a clear blueprint in Shakur Stevenson’s showing against Teofimo. Teofimo relies on a predictable pattern. He presses forward like an incoming tide to unleash combinations before resetting straight back. That approach gives a poised counterpuncher like Catterall clean opportunities to time him. Teofimo risks losing the belt before Ryan ever gets him in the ring.

If Teofimo chooses to vacate instead, the matchup with Ryan loses its title prestige and strips Teofimo of negotiating power. Ryan generates massive arena business on his own name. Lopez relies on Ryan to produce a career-high purse.

Waiting on Teofimo introduces ring rust for Ryan. Lengthy layoffs have disrupted Ryan’s timing throughout his career, and sanctioning body disputes rarely resolve quickly. A December fight keeps him sharp while cashing another substantial check.

Pitbull Cruz brings action appeal, yet remains vulnerable to Ryan’s weapons. The short pressure fighter moves forward behind an earmuff guard and lunges inside. Ryan possesses the straight right to split that defense and the check left hook to catch Cruz in mid-leap. That physical contrast grows sharper once Ryan hydrates up into middleweight territory on fight night.

Teofimo delivers the steeper tactical hurdle. He possesses the lateral agility to circle away from Ryan’s hook, the upper body slip to evade incoming right hands, and the counterpunching ability to punish an upright target.

Mannix viewed Cruz as a distraction on the road to Lopez. Catterall stands as the real roadblock. Ryan can face Cruz in December while Lopez sorts through his WBA mess. If Teofimo still possesses the belt when the dust clears, Madison Square Garden will still be waiting.

The WBA already shredded its own credibility by sanctioning Teofimo against Rolly Romero in the first place. Giving an immediate shot at a secondary belt to a fighter coming straight off a wide points loss to Shakur Stevenson made a mockery of the ratings. The only justification offered was the commercial value of putting two loud talkers on pay-per-view.

Now Gilberto Mendoza is caught in the trap he created. That July 9 message to Catterall, explicitly telling him he would get the winner of Rolly versus Teofimo within 180 days, puts the WBA president on the record. Matchroom’s legal team has documented proof that Catterall took the risk, beat Shakhram Giyasov, and earned his status in a sanctioned eliminator.

From a sporting standpoint, letting Teofimo bypass Catterall looks terrible. It signals that mandatory positions only exist for contenders who lack the leverage to be ignored. Teofimo arguing that his name was not on the original paperwork is classic promoter double-talk. Mandatory obligations belong to the championship belt, not the individual holding it. If a title changes hands, the new champion inherits the baggage attached to the hardware.

Despite how ugly it looks, the WBA will almost certainly look for an escape hatch if Ryan Garcia and Lopez finalize terms. Sanctioning bodies operate on percentages of total fight purses. A percentage of a Ryan Garcia pay-per-view at Madison Square Garden generates massive revenue for the WBA. A low-profile mandatory defense between Lopez and Catterall in Manchester or New York pays a tiny fraction of that amount.

Sports.title: David Benavidez Eyes Andy Ruiz for Heavyweight Debut
Sports.content:
David Benavidez is mapping out a multi-division campaign that his team hopes will culminate in a heavyweight appearance against Andy Ruiz Jr. José Benavidez Sr. laid out a scenario where David campaigns at cruiserweight against Michal Cieslak and Jai Opetaia, drops to light heavyweight for Dmitry Bivol or Artur Beterbiev, and then jumps into the heavyweight division.

“After that, we would love to make a fight with Andy Ruiz. We’re just dreaming here, daydreaming, but those are the fights that I think are very possible to make. Imagine David Benavidez and Andy Ruiz. Andy is a great fighter. My heart is with him, and he’s like family to me, but I believe he would love the same, an opportunity to fight the Mexican Monster. For us, it would be a great opportunity,” said Jose Sr. to ProBox TV.

Jumping between three weight classes demands an enormous physical toll. David would have to pack on bulk to trade punches with cruiserweights, strip off 25 pounds to make the 175-pound limit, and then rebuild his body for heavyweight. Modern fighters rarely ping-pong across weight classes because stripping away functional muscle ruins stamina, drains punch resistance, and deadens a fighter’s legs.

Targeting Ruiz reveals a desire for name recognition over actual heavyweight danger. Ruiz carries brand value, quick combinations, and strong appeal in the southwestern market. He also stands barely six feet tall and lacks the reach of legitimate heavyweights.

Ruiz returned from a two-year layoff and suffered a defeat against Damian Knyba. By the time David finishes this proposed multi-belt tour, Ruiz will be pushing 40 with extensive periods of ring rust. Facing that diminished version provides David a heavyweight victory without the terror of sharing a ring with a massive, six-foot-six puncher.

Reaching that point assumes David survives the cruiserweight division, which looks like pure fantasy. Opetaia is not a stepping stone. The Australian operates with elite lateral movement, explosive power, and precise timing. David had uncomfortable moments handling the physical pressure and punches of Oleksandr Gvozdyk at light heavyweight. Opetaia possesses far more destructive force at 200 pounds and has the tools to dismantle David before any heavyweight plans materialize.

The promotional hurdles make the blueprint even more detached from reality. Coordinating multiple sanctioning bodies, rival promoters, and separate network platforms across three weight classes takes years. David risks burning through his athletic peak waiting for theoretical fights that may never happen.

José Sr. openly called the idea daydreaming, yet floating Ruiz exposes the underlying strategy. Team Benavidez wants heavyweight credit without taking heavyweight risks, targeting an aging, undersized former champion instead of the division’s genuine giants.

Counting on Ruiz to rebuild credibility by stringing together wins over the next couple of years ignores everything he has shown inside and outside the ring. Against Jarrell Miller, Ruiz could barely muster the work rate to stay competitive, struggling through long stretches where his punch output disappeared. Following that up with a lackluster performance and a loss to Damian Knyba confirmed that the hunger, conditioning, and explosiveness that defined his upset win in 2019 are long gone. Put him in with any durable, busy heavyweight right now, and he drops another decision simply by being outworked.

The financial reality makes the idea of a comeback even more absurd. Ruiz made life-changing money from the Anthony Joshua bouts and has zero financial urgency to run through grueling training camps or take punishment. When a heavyweight has millions in the bank and only fights once every year or two, the fire never comes back. Expecting him to suddenly become active, stay disciplined, and beat legitimate contenders while David Benavidez runs a marathon through cruiserweight and light heavyweight is wishful thinking.

If this matchup ever happens, Team Benavidez will not be getting a resurgent former champion coming off a hot streak. They will be buying the shell of a recognizable name who is happy to cash one final paycheck before walking away for good. That makes the commercial payoff far smaller than José Sr. envisions, because boxing fans can easily see through a cash grab against a washed-up opponent.

Sports.title: Janibek Alimkhanuly’s Canelo Alvarez Plan Requires Statement Knockout
Sports.content:
Janibek Alimkhanuly sees the vacant WBO super middleweight title as his route to Canelo Alvarez. Winning it will not be enough. He needs a violent performance that gives boxing fans a reason to demand the unification.

“Everyone knows I’m not interested in the money. I’m ready! I’m also ready to see the news that he’s vacating the title. I just need that title. Then I have to unify with Canelo. That’s it!”

Janibek posted that message on X last Thursday following the purse bid for his ordered fight with Hamzah Sheeraz. Queensberry won with an offer of $1,001,809, but Sheeraz surrendered the WBO title shortly afterward. Janibek returned Monday with another message: “Brother, why not Janibek vs Canelo? 😎”

The WBO must first choose his opponent. Diego Pacheco and Jacob Bank are among the leading candidates, and Pacheco would make Janibek earn every bit of his new position. The 6’4″ contender has the reach, power, and natural size to test whether Janibek’s punch resistance belongs at 168.

Janibek cannot merely edge Pacheco from the outside. He would need to cut off the ring, close the distance, and stop a younger super middleweight to prove his power traveled with him.

Even then, the business case works against him. Canelo has never allowed sanctioning bodies to control his schedule. David Benavidez had an interim belt, substantial public support, and years of pressure behind him. None of it produced the fight.

Janibek offers even less commercial incentive. He is a dangerous southpaw with heavy hands and extensive amateur schooling, but he lacks a large American pay-per-view audience. That makes him a severe physical risk without the purse Canelo expects from taking one.

Canelo has defeated southpaws Billy Joe Saunders and John Ryder since his difficult 2014 fight with Erislandy Lara. Janibek presents a different version of that stance. He is more compact, hits harder, and looks for damaging counters instead of surviving through movement. Canelo must also defeat WBC champion Christian Mbilli on October 31. At 36, Canelo is nearing the final stage of his career and will favor stadium events, major paydays, and carefully selected farewell fights over collecting every available belt.

Janibek cannot force his way onto that schedule. Knocking out a credible WBO opponent would at least make leaving him off much harder to defend. Taking on Pacheco, Sadjo, or Bank for the vacant strap means Janibek must instantly solve elite 168-pounders without a warm-up bout.

The odds of both men surviving those respective hurdles to meet in a unification clash look slim. Alvarez facing Mbilli after a full year out of the ring is a risky fight for a superstar on the decline. Against Terence Crawford, Canelo looked heavy, flat-footed, and completely devoid of the sharp reaction time that once made his upper-body movement and counter-punching elite-grade.

Mbilli is the worst stylistic matchup for someone in Canelo’s state: he is relentless, throws punches in volume from awkward angles, and doesn’t care about taking shots to land his own. Canelo is not suddenly going to regain the lateral movement or snap needed to keep Mbilli off him for twelve rounds.

The division jump from 160 to 168 pounds is brutal for Janibek. At middleweight, he could intimidate opponents with power and technical skills. At super middleweight, he’ll face naturally bigger, harder-hitting, and far more seasoned opponents than anyone on his middleweight record.

Sports.title: Hearn Risks Matchroom’s Future for Aging Joshua
Sports.content:
Eddie Hearn may have secured Anthony Joshua’s preferred country for the Tyson Fury fight, but Roy Jones Jr. believes the Matchroom promoter has damaged his position with the people controlling boxing’s richest events.

Joshua and Fury had agreed to fight November 20 at Madison Square Garden. Hearn resisted the New York venue because Joshua’s contract required the contest to take place in Britain. The heavyweight clash is now likely to land at Principality Stadium in Cardiff on December 11.

That gives Hearn a victory he can sell to the British public, but the reported 2 a.m. local start removes much of its meaning. Seventy thousand paying spectators may be asked to remain inside the stadium until early morning so Netflix can show the fight during American prime time.

If Jones is correct that American viewers have little interest in Fury–Joshua, the compromise becomes harder to defend. Britain provides the crowd, ticket money and atmosphere while the broadcast schedule caters to an audience that Jones says does not care.

Jones applauded Hearn for resisting the combined pressure from Turki Alalshikh, Sela, Netflix, Dana White, TKO and Team Fury. He also offered a much darker forecast for Matchroom.

“Hearn has won a battle, but he’s gonna lose the war. I just think it’s because Turki has enough money to do whatever he wants to do. Whoever has his ear is gonna win the war, because he’s got the money to keep it going. But my hat goes off to Eddie for fighting, because Eddie knows that war is not the best thing for boxing,” Jones told Parimatch Slots Site, via BoxingScene.

The concern reaches beyond a disagreement over one venue. Alalshikh has the financial resources to outlast any traditional promoter. If he decides TKO and Frank Warren are easier partners, Matchroom can be removed from major cards without leaving the Saudi operation short of alternatives.

Warren has remained aligned with the Riyadh group while showing flexibility over the Fury–Joshua date and location. That may leave Queensberry better placed for future Saudi events as Hearn returns to a far more limited DAZN schedule.

Dana White and TKO present another danger. White wants a more centralized boxing structure with tighter control over fighters and purses. Hearn has built his reputation by securing the largest possible payments for his boxers. The two approaches were always likely to collide, and this dispute may have given TKO another reason to work around Matchroom.

Hearn has made that stand for a 36-year-old Joshua whose career is nearing its conclusion. Joshua helped build Matchroom Boxing into an international company, so the promoter’s loyalty is understandable. However, Jaron Ennis, Diego Pacheco, Conor Benn and Matchroom’s younger fighters will need access to major financial opportunities long after Joshua retires.

It is too early to state that Hearn’s relationship with Alalshikh is finished. Neither side has announced a permanent split. Jones nevertheless sees the imbalance clearly. Hearn enforced Joshua’s contract and preserved the British venue, but he challenged a group with enough money, fighters, and promotional partners to continue without him.

Joshua may receive the home fight he demanded. Matchroom’s younger stable may inherit its cost. Hearn is playing a dangerous game that makes very little sense over the long haul. When you strip away the promotional spin about honoring contracts and protecting home fans, the strategy looks remarkably short-sighted.

Joshua is thirty-six years old and standing on the final chapter of his career. Whether he has two fights left or three, Matchroom cannot hitch its wagon to him much longer. By drawing a line in the sand against Turki Alalshikh, Sela, Netflix, and the TKO group, Hearn is spending massive institutional equity on an asset that is depreciating by the month. Once Joshua hangs up the gloves, Matchroom has to live in the boxing world that remains. That world is funded almost entirely by Riyadh.

If Alalshikh decides Matchroom is too difficult to deal with, the younger talent Hearn needs to build around will pay the price. Top prospects and champions will not stay loyal to an outfit that is shut out of the deepest pockets in combat sports.

The Cardiff compromise exposes the flaw in Hearn’s victory lap. Promising British supporters a home showcase only to force seventy thousand fans to sit in a stadium until three in the morning completely guts the value of fighting in the UK.

Having tens of thousands of people spill out into the freezing, wet Welsh rain at 3:30 or 4:00 AM with shut-down public transit is an absolute logistical disaster for the live audience. It turns the live crowd into background props for a North American television broadcast.

Staging the bout at Madison Square Garden would have been far cleaner. A direct flight across the Atlantic takes about seven hours. Die-hard British fight fans are used to traveling for major Vegas and New York fights anyway, and the rest of the domestic audience could have watched from the comfort of their living rooms at 4:00 AM instead of freezing in Cardiff.

Hearn won the contractual dispute, but alienating sovereign money, major streaming partners, and powerful promotional allies over an unworkable domestic compromise leaves Matchroom with far more to lose than to gain.

Sports.title: Can David Morrell Recover at Light Heavyweight?
Sports.content:
David Morrell has disappeared from the boxing conversation since Zak Chelli stopped him in the 10th round on May 9. Once presented as a future star at super middleweight, the Cuban now sits at 12-2 with no confirmed return date and serious questions about his future at 175 pounds.

Chelli accepted the fight on two weeks’ notice and was trailing before hurting Morrell in the ninth and finishing him with 36 seconds left in the final round. It was not merely a shocking defeat. It exposed a technical weakness that had followed Morrell throughout his professional career.

When pressured, Morrell retreats in straight lines until his heels reach the edge of the ring. He then squares his upper body, raises both gloves, and waits for the attack to end.

The guard protects parts of his head, but widening his torso gives opponents access to his liver and ribs. He also provides no angle for an escape. Instead of stepping around an orthodox fighter’s lead foot, Morrell remains directly in front of him.

David Benavidez exploited that behavior over 12 rounds in February 2025. Morrell dropped Benavidez in the 11th, but those isolated successes could not erase the long stretches he spent absorbing combinations along the ropes.

Chelli found the same opening. Once Morrell’s legs faded, the guard became a hiding place rather than an active defense.

Morrell remains dangerous when he has room to select his shots. His straight left hand, counter right hook, and short two-punch bursts are fast enough to punish careless entries. The trouble begins when an opponent survives the first attack. Morrell rarely follows with the sustained combinations needed to hold the center of the ring. His style still carries the rhythm of amateur boxing: land the cleaner single shot, reset and wait for another opening. Professional pressure fighters do not always grant that reset.

An opponent willing to walk through one or two hard punches can force Morrell backward and beat him through activity. Morrell does not have a developed inside game that allows him to fight for position once the distance has disappeared.

Elite fighters who become trapped along the ropes usually clinch, pin an arm or turn the attacker before leaving. Morrell does little of that.

He stands behind his forearms and allows opponents to complete their combinations. Even when most of the punches strike his gloves, judges see one fighter attacking and the other merely surviving.

That passivity is more exhausting at light heavyweight. Morrell was physically stronger than most of his opposition at 168 pounds. At 175, naturally larger fighters can drive their weight into him and force his legs to support both bodies.

Holding a turtle guard under that pressure drains the shoulders, back, and thighs. It helps explain why Morrell’s energy vanished so rapidly against Chelli in the ninth and 10th rounds. Morrell reportedly relocated to Orlando and changed his training setup after the Chelli defeat. A new camp will only help if it changes his reactions when another fighter presses him.

He needs lateral escape steps, an offensive clinch, and combinations long enough to make opponents reconsider walking forward. Returning to super middleweight would reduce the physical burden, although making 168 again may no longer be practical.

Matchmaking presents another issue. Morrell remains too powerful to become an easy opponent for a rising prospect, but his two defeats have stripped away much of his bargaining power. A soft return fight will bring criticism, while another aggressive volume puncher may push him farther from the top level. Morrell is only 28, and his speed, power, and amateur background still give him valuable tools.

His future depends on accepting that the defense which carried him through 168 pounds does not work against strong light heavyweights. If he returns with the same straight-line retreat and stationary high guard, Chelli’s victory will no longer look like an isolated upset. It will look like a blueprint.

Ghana News.title: Ghana’s MSMEs: Burdened by regulation and overtaxed; why the system isn’t working
Ghana News.content:
Ghana's MSMEs face a profound policy paradox: while tax reforms at the national level have been unprecedented in ambition, the fragmented and opaque regulatory enforcement at the municipal level constitutes a "hidden tax" far more lethal than nominal tax rates. Whatever relief the reforms offer is consumed by compliance costs long before it reaches the small businesses that need it most.

On paper, Ghana's tax reforms look promising. The Value Added Tax Act (Act 1151), effective 2026, reduced the effective VAT rate from approximately 21.9% to 20%, abolished the 1% COVID-19 levy, and raised the VAT registration threshold from GHS 200,000 to GHS 750,000 in annual turnover. The Finance Minister claimed these measures would return some GHS 6 billion to households and businesses in 2026 and reduce the cost of doing business by 5%.

Yet a vast "temperature gap" exists between these paper promises and what MSMEs actually experience.

The Backbone of the Economy, Struggling to Survive

Ghana's MSMEs are the undisputed backbone of the economy. According to a 2026 study by the Institute for Liberty and Policy Innovation (ILAPI) covering 600 enterprises, MSMEs account for approximately 92% of all businesses and contribute nearly 70% of GDP. Data from the Ghana Statistical Service shows that the informal sector represented 92% of the 1.8 million private enterprises in 2024, employing about 69% of the workforce.

But this massive group's survival is precarious. The MSME failure rate disclosed in parliamentary debate stands at a staggering 50%, with startup success rates at just 20%. Data from the UN Capital Development Fund further shows that nearly 70% of MSMEs collapse within their first five years.

The Real Killer: The Municipal "Compliance Maze"

For most MSMEs, what kills them is often not the tax law itself. Research by ILAPI reveals the true cost of the regulatory ecosystem at the municipal level: the average cost of obtaining a permit from a Metropolitan, Municipal, or District Assembly (MMDA) is GHS 1,275, while licence fees average GHS 1,600, with some businesses paying as much as GHS 3,000. Business registration itself costs an average of GHS 1,030.

But these figures are only the tip of the iceberg. The core problem ILAPI identifies is institutional fragmentation: overlapping institutional mandates, excessive documentation requirements, opaque procedures, and inconsistent enforcement together constitute a "middleman tax." Because regulatory agencies are inaccessible and opaque, businesses are forced to rely on unofficial intermediaries to achieve compliance costs that never appear in any official statistic.

A 2024 study by the Nordic Africa Institute on the carbon emissions tax provides a powerful cautionary tale. The overall compliance rate was just 15%, dropping to 4% for micro-enterprises. Nearly 60% of businesses explicitly refused the tax, with acceptance at only 11%. The failure was not due to excessive rates; micro-enterprises actually bore a burden of only about 8% of revenue. The real barrier was the absence of compliance infrastructure: businesses needed to install equipment to measure and report greenhouse gas emissions, an entirely unrealistic burden for micro-enterprises that lack even basic bookkeeping. The tax was hastily abolished in April 2025. The lesson is clear: a tax, however well-designed, whose compliance requirements exceed the target group's capacity to execute, will result only in widespread avoidance and ultimate failure.

Why Reform Dividends Are Being "Intercepted"

The 2026 VAT reforms are technically rational. Reintegrating NHIL and GETFund into the VAT base while allowing input tax deductions does eliminate the long-standing cascading effect. Raising the threshold to GHS 750,000 theoretically excludes a large number of micro-enterprises from the complex VAT system.

But the problem is this: for micro-enterprises with extremely tight cash flow, the meaning of "deductible" is limited. They often lack sufficient output tax to genuinely benefit from deductions, and may instead face intensified cash flow pressure from having to advance input tax. The Ghana Revenue Authority has itself acknowledged that some traders raised prices because they failed to exclude non-deductible input tax under the old regime, indicating serious friction in the reform's transmission mechanism.

Professor Godfred Bokpin of the University of Ghana Business School has pointed out that even at 20%, Ghana's VAT rate remains "too high." He argues that 18% is Ghana's optimal rate and warns that under the AfCFTA framework, high VAT rates incentivise smuggling from neighbouring countries such as Nigeria, where the rate is just 7.5%.

An Overlooked Perspective: The "Punishment" of Formalisation

The Ghana Revenue Authority claims Ghana's tax-to-GDP ratio stands at just 13%, among the lowest in sub-Saharan Africa. But this macro figure obscures a critical structural problem: formal-sector SMEs actually bear a heavier tax burden than their informal counterparts.

This "formalisation penalty" directly erodes the incentive for businesses to enter the formal sector: if compliance means higher taxes and more complex administrative burdens, while the benefits of better public services and access to finance remain unclear, rational businesses will naturally choose to remain informal.

The Erosion of Fairness and the Loss of Compliance Willingness

The effectiveness of a tax system depends not only on rates but on taxpayers' perception of fairness. The Nordic Africa Institute survey found that Ghanaian businesses rated the fairness of the tax system at an average of just 51 out of 100. Informal enterprises perceived the lowest fairness, at only 45. When compliance cannot deliver perceptible benefits, such as better public services or a more level playing field, it can only be experienced as pure extraction.

The Way Forward: A "Municipal-Level" Revolution

The core paradox facing Ghana's MSMEs is this: the tax system at the national level is striving to modernise, but the regulatory ecosystem at the local level remains pre-modern.

The comprehensive Income Tax Act revision and Customs Act reform currently before Parliament are directionally correct: simplification, digitalisation, alignment with international standards. But these macro reforms cannot automatically resolve the fragmentation at the municipal level.

What is truly needed is a "structural surgery" targeting the local regulatory ecosystem: mandating the consolidation of municipal licensing procedures, establishing a unified digital platform, publishing all fee schedules, and severely punishing rent-seeking behaviour. ILAPI's recommendation for a unified digital platform allowing businesses to apply for multiple permits at once is a pragmatic direction, but it requires political will to overcome the entrenched interests of municipal agencies.

The word that recurred in Parliament's MSME Day commemorative statement was "handholding", not just providing loans, but offering management training, financial guidance, and strategic planning support. This hints at a deeper recognition: what MSMEs face is not merely a tax burden problem, but a systemic mismatch between capacity building and the institutional environment.

Otherwise, whatever tax relief is offered at the national level will be consumed long before it reaches the corner shop or the small repair workshop.

-

Authored by Kweku Hammond, Snr Sales & Marketing Consultant/ Faculty Nova Business School Africa.

Ghana News.title: Patience Akyianu, former Barclays Bank Ghana MD and Hollard Group CEO, reported dead
Ghana News.content:
The former Managing Director of Barclays Bank Ghana and Group Chief Executive Officer of Hollard Ghana, Patience Enyonam Akyianu, has reportedly passed away.

Her reported death marks the loss of a prominent figure in Ghana’s banking and insurance industries, where she built a career spanning more than two decades and held senior leadership positions.

The circumstances surrounding her reported death have not been independently confirmed. But the CEO Network Ghana, which confirmed her demise in a statement, said, "It is with profound sadness and heavy hearts that we announce the passing of our dear friend and distinguished CEO, Patience Akyianu, Group CEO of Hollard Holdings."

"Her passing is a deeply painful loss to the business community and to all of us who knew and cherished her. We extend our heartfelt condolences to her family, colleagues, friends and loved ones. May God grant them strength and comfort during this difficult time. Further details will be shared as received from the family. May her gentle soul rest in perfect peace", it said.

From banking to insurance leadership

Mrs Akyianu built much of her career in banking, serving in senior financial and executive positions before her appointment as Managing Director of Barclays Bank Ghana.

She previously worked as Finance Director at the bank before becoming its Managing Director, a position she held for five years.

According to a profile published by the Ghana Stock Exchange, she had more than 26 years of experience in banking and finance, including 17 years in the banking industry before transitioning to insurance in 2018.

Her academic qualifications included an MBA in Finance and a Bachelor of Science degree in Business Administration, specialising in Accounting, both from the University of Ghana Business School.

She was also a certified professional accountant and a member of the Institute of Chartered Accountants, Ghana.

Hollard Ghana’s pioneering Group CEO

In October 2018, Mrs Akyianu left Barclays Bank Ghana to become the Chief Executive Officer of Hollard Ghana Holdings, taking charge of the newly established insurance group.

Her appointment followed Hollard’s expansion in Ghana, bringing together Hollard Insurance Ghana, formerly Metropolitan Insurance, and Hollard Life Assurance Ghana.

She became the group’s first CEO, leading its efforts to expand its presence in Ghana’s insurance market and develop consumer-focused insurance solutions.

In a 2021 reflection on her leadership journey, Mrs Akyianu described the move from banking to insurance as a leap of faith.

She said she had been attracted by the opportunity to build Hollard into a household name in Ghana, despite moving into an industry in which she had relatively little experience.

“I saw a great brand with a great purpose, a great vision, and a great business ethos,” she wrote.

She described her years at Hollard as a period of transformation, innovation and growth, while acknowledging the challenges of building a business in a new sector.

A career marked by industry recognition

Mrs Akyianu’s contributions to Ghana’s financial services sector earned her several professional honours.

In May 2025, she received the Millennium Excellence Award for Finance and Capital Market Excellence at the Manhyia Palace in Kumasi.

The award recognised her leadership at Barclays Bank Ghana and Hollard Ghana, as well as her contribution to the development of the finance and capital markets.

The citation highlighted her role in the adoption of International Financial Reporting Standards at Standard Chartered Bank and Barclays Bank Ghana, saying it had enhanced transparency and discipline in the banking sector.

She was also recognised for her contributions to leadership and mentorship.

Beyond her executive roles, Mrs Akyianu served on corporate boards and was a founding member of the Executive Women Network and the International Women’s Forum, Ghana.

Commitment to inclusion and customer-focused insurance

At Hollard Ghana, Mrs Akyianu championed efforts to make insurance more accessible to individuals and businesses.

The company introduced products and partnerships aimed at reaching underserved customers and expanding access to insurance.

Among these was the Asomdwee insurance product, launched in partnership with the Ghana Enterprises Agency in 2021 to provide tailored insurance cover for micro, small and medium-sized enterprises.

She described the initiative as part of a broader effort to support business owners and protect their assets against unexpected events.

Her leadership also coincided with Hollard’s investment in new distribution channels, digital insurance solutions and customer experience.

Ghana News.title: Mahama pushes ‘health sovereignty’ agenda, says Global South needs control over resources
Ghana News.content:
President John Dramani Mahama has called for a fundamental shift in the way global health cooperation is structured, insisting that countries in the Global South cannot truly own their health systems without control over their financing, resources and production capacity.

He made the call in New York on Monday, September 21, after launching the High-Level Panel Report of the Accra Reset, titled “A Sovereign Future for Health,” on the sidelines of the 81st United Nations General Assembly.

The report sets out proposals for reforming the global health architecture around stronger national and regional capabilities, greater domestic ownership and more accountable partnerships with international development institutions.

President Mahama said the initiative was aimed at moving developing countries away from a model in which critical health programmes remain heavily dependent on external funding and decisions made outside their jurisdictions.

“One year ago, through the Accra Reset, we rejected the idea that the health, dignity, and future of our people should remain perpetually tied to foreign donor magnanimity,” he said in a Facebook post announcing the report.

He argued that the concept of “country ownership” had often failed to give countries meaningful control over the resources and decisions shaping their health systems.

“To put it plainly, we were handed a broken cauldron and asked to own a soup cooked entirely in someone else’s kitchen,” he said.

“Today, through the Accra Reset, we declare unequivocally that there can be NO ownership without control.”

Mahama links sovereignty to accountability

While advocating greater control for developing countries, President Mahama said sovereignty must be matched by stronger domestic accountability.

He said Ghana’s own reform agenda would focus on tightening fiscal management, fighting corruption and strengthening local productive capacity.

“However, sovereignty is not a blank check. If we demand control, we must earn it through uncompromising domestic accountability,” he said.

According to him, the Resetting Ghana agenda includes efforts to strengthen fiscal management and build local industrial capacity, particularly in the pharmaceutical sector.

He said the objective was to enable Ghanaian pharmaceutical companies to manufacture essential medicines locally rather than depend excessively on foreign assistance.

The High-Level Panel report similarly proposes stronger regional health manufacturing, coordinated procurement and commodity security, sustainable financing transitions and independent mechanisms to track governments and development partners against agreed commitments.

Health sovereignty focused on maternal mortality

President Mahama said health had been chosen as the first major area of focus, with particular attention to maternal mortality across sub-Saharan Africa.

He pointed to initiatives including Mother Africa and Business United for Mothers, Babies and Youth (BUMBY) as part of efforts to translate the commitments into practical interventions for women, children and young people.

“We are selecting health as our first battleground with a direct focus on ending the unacceptable maternal mortality rates across Sub-Saharan Africa,” he said.

The Accra Reset’s Full Circle programme in New York placed the health report at the centre of its discussions on a new global development bargain, alongside initiatives on maternal and child health, skills, fair deal-making and shared prosperity.

New global health bargain

President Mahama said the report provides a framework for a new global bargain based on three principles: ownership backed by real control over resources and production capabilities; cooperation built around human dignity and equal partnerships; and domestic accountability to ensure public resources serve citizens.

“The report sets out a clear path for a New Global Bargain built on Ownership backed by real control over our resources and production capabilities, Cooperation defined by human dignity, [and] mature, equal partnerships with global allies, and Absolute domestic accountability to ensure public resources serve our citizens down to the last pesewa,” he said.

The High-Level Panel's proposals include a country-led “one-stop” health compact, sustainable financing transitions, stronger regional institutions, regional health manufacturing, improved procurement systems and independent follow-up on commitments. It proposes that independent follow-up begin within six months, while country-led compacts should be developed within 12 months.

The report does not call for an abrupt end to international assistance. Instead, it proposes a managed transition in which external support protects essential services while countries progressively build stronger national and regional health capabilities.

President Mahama expressed gratitude to former Nigerian President Olusegun Obasanjo, former Liberian President Ellen Johnson Sirleaf and former Costa Rican President Laura Chinchilla, as well as the High-Level Panel’s co-chairs and other partners, for their contributions to the initiative.

Ghana News.title: Mahama: We are reforming systems, fighting corruption and improving use of public funds
Ghana News.content:
President John Dramani Mahama says his administration is reforming Ghana’s governance systems to strengthen accountability, fight corruption and ensure public resources are used more efficiently for the benefit of citizens.

He said the government was reviewing systems and financial arrangements within the public sector to improve transparency and ensure that public funds were channelled towards their intended purposes.

President Mahama made the remarks at the Accra Reset event in New York, held on the sidelines of the 81st United Nations General Assembly under the theme, “Full Circle: Making Global Development Work Again.”

He said reforming Ghana’s governance systems remained a key priority, particularly in the areas of accountability, public finances and the management of national resources.

“In Ghana, we are reforming our systems. We are making government more accountable. We are fighting corruption, and we are making more efficient use of our resources than we did in the past,” he said.

President Mahama cited the decision to uncap funding for the National Health Insurance Scheme (NHIS) as one of the first steps taken by his administration after assuming office.

He criticised the previous government’s management of statutory funds, arguing that the system had restricted the resources available to the NHIS and other statutory institutions.

“One of the first steps I took was to uncap the National Health Insurance. And what the previous government had done was to put a cap on all statutory funds,” he said.

According to President Mahama, funds exceeding the prescribed percentage of the national budget were transferred into the Consolidated Fund, which he alleged was then used largely for programmes intended to secure political support.

“And if they exceeded a certain percentage of the budget, the excess funds went into the Consolidated Fund and government used it mostly for programmes that would buy political patronage and put them in a better position to win the elections,” he said.

The Accra Reset event brought together stakeholders to discuss global development, governance, financing and the need to reshape development systems to make them more responsive to the needs of countries and their populations.

Ghana News.title: Catholic Bishops welcome task force to tackle drug menace, acknowledge inter-agency efforts
Ghana News.content:
The Ghana Catholic Bishops’ Conference has welcomed President John Dramani Mahama’s decision to establish an inter-agency task force to tackle the movement of narcotic drugs through the country’s ports, airports and borders.

The Bishops also commended the Narcotics Control Commission (NACOC) and other state agencies for their efforts to combat illicit drug trafficking and abuse in Ghana.

In a statement, the Conference said the measures were important steps towards strengthening Ghana’s response to the growing threat of drug trafficking and abuse.

The Bishops called for sustained collaboration among state institutions and international partners to disrupt trafficking networks and prevent Ghana from being used as a transit point for illicit drugs.

Their comments follow the recent seizure of nearly 3.9 tonnes of cocaine in France, allegedly concealed in a container of plastic waste from Ghana.

The Conference said the seizure underscored the need for stronger surveillance, accountability and coordination at Ghana’s ports, airports and borders.

It called for a thorough investigation to establish how such a large consignment allegedly passed through legitimate commercial channels.

The Bishops also urged continued cooperation between Ghanaian authorities and their French counterparts to uncover the full extent of the trafficking network connected to the seizure.

Bishops call for trafficking networks to be dismantled

The Conference said the Dunkirk seizure should be viewed within the context of a wider national challenge, citing other narcotics interceptions linked to Ghana in recent years.

It expressed concern over the alleged involvement of people in positions of trust, including public officials and, regrettably, some members of the Church.

“The fight must include anyone who abuses public trust to facilitate the movement of illicit substances,” the statement said.

The Bishops further urged investigators to look beyond couriers and identify the financiers and principal traffickers behind the trade.

“A pattern in which couriers are prosecuted while the networks that finance them escape scrutiny is the failure any credible national response must overcome,” the Conference said.

The Conference described illicit drug trafficking and abuse as a serious national concern and a profound moral crisis, urging coordinated and sustained action to address the problem.

Ghana News.title: Tamale: 5 arrested over suspected drug activities; police seize pistols, narcotics
Ghana News.content:
The Northern Regional Police Command has arrested five persons and seized firearms, ammunition, suspected narcotics and other items during an intelligence-led operation at the Tamale Aboabo Scrap Area.

The operation was conducted on Monday, September 21, 2026, by the Regional Special Operations Team, popularly known as RED MARIA, following what police described as credible intelligence on suspected drug-related and other criminal activities in the area.

The suspects are Ibrahim Issahaku, 39; Mohamed John, 28; Mohamed Nawas, 25; Mohamed Osman Awal, 41; and Kwame Boateng, 28.

According to the police, Mohamed John and Mohamed Nawas are suspected drug users, while Kwame Boateng is suspected of dealing in narcotics.

Mohamed Osman Awal, identified as the owner of the scrap business at the location, is alleged to have been harbouring drug peddlers on the premises.

Firearms, suspected narcotics seized

A search of Ibrahim Issahaku’s residence led to the recovery of two foreign-made pistols, two rounds of 9mm ammunition, a parcel of suspected Indian hemp and GH¢1,880 in cash.

Police also recovered GH¢18,825 concealed inside Kwame Boateng’s motorcycle, which they suspect to be proceeds from the sale of narcotic drugs.

Other items seized during the operation included 123 wraps of suspected Indian hemp, 12 sachets of 1mg Rohypnol, seven sachets of 250mg Tramadol, 111 wraps of suspected “ashes” and three motorbikes.

The suspects and exhibits have since been handed over to the Regional Drug Law Enforcement Unit (RDLEU) for further investigation and necessary action.

The Northern Regional Police Command says it will continue to undertake intelligence-led operations to disrupt illicit drug trafficking, drug use and other related criminal activities in the region.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”
