World.title: Joosep Vimm: It's time to fix Estonia's short-term rental market
World.content:
Estonia's failure to regulate short-term rentals is costing the state tax revenue, distorting competition in the accommodations sector and undermining the quality of life in Tallinn's Old Town, Joosep Vimm argues.

The Ministry of Economic Affairs and Communications is burying its head in the sand again. Every year, millions of euros in tax revenue from short-term rental apartments go uncollected. Yet the ministry has postponed making decisions under the guise of conducting yet another analysis. Shall we do another study? Maybe set up a committee, too? In reality, no progress has been made over the past four years. The problems are only piling up.

When I served as Tallinn deputy mayor, I pushed to bring order to the place of short-term rental apartments in the market. It was then and largely remains today a black market that distorts competition and causes other problems as well.

In 2023, I took part in the Ministry of Economic Affairs and Communications' tourism roundtable where the various parties involved acknowledged the need for change. Then-Minister Tiit Riisalo and ministry officials were eventually forced to concede that the issue needed to be addressed. However, they wanted to wait and see what impact newly enacted EU legislation covering various intermediary platforms would have and to conduct yet another thorough analysis of the situation.

At the time, market participants were optimistic that the ministry wanted to tackle the problem. My sense, which I also expressed to several of those involved, was that the ministry would use the analysis process to smother the issue and consign it to a drawer. Here we are three years later and that prediction has come true. In fact, the scenario is even worse. The ministry is explicitly saying that no regulation is needed.

In reality, regulation is very much needed, both from the perspective of Estonia as a whole and, more specifically, Tallinn. Three main problems have long been in need of a solution: lost tax revenue, unfair competition in the accommodations market and the living environment in Tallinn's Old Town.

An estimated one-fifth of Tallinn's accommodation beds are in short-term rental apartments. Since there is no functioning registry of these properties, we essentially do not know who these (potential) taxpayers are or exactly how much tax revenue is being lost.

Estimates vary. The Estonian Hotel and Restaurant Association has calculated that the state is missing out on nearly €50 million in tax revenue. Maybe it is a little more, maybe a little less, but to quote Peeter Oja's legendary character Kert Ämmapets: "We're not talking about 3.50 here." In light of the state budget deficit, money is simply being left on the table. And supposedly there is no money for raising teachers' salaries, either.

When people talk about the free market, they often forget, accidentally or deliberately, that a genuinely free market is ensured by fair competition. Market participants operating on equal terms and under the same rules compete and generate profits — not in a free-for-all where some gain an advantage through unfair practices. An honest business model should not be built on failing to pay taxes.

Yet we have a significant number of accommodation providers — that is, short-term rental providers — that the law does not even treat as accommodation businesses. There are no standards and no guest registration requirements, creating an unfair competitive advantage in pricing because providers can save money by avoiding taxes.

In addition, residents of Tallinn's Old Town have for years raised concerns about the rapid deterioration in the quality of their living environment. The everyday problems associated with short-term rental apartments have crossed a critical threshold, leaving permanent residents without a livable environment. Each individual problem has to be dealt with separately, but by then the guests in the neighboring apartment have already left and the owners simply shrug their shoulders.

There is no systemic solution. As a result, more and more residents of Tallinn's Old Town are under pressure to give up. They, too, decide to move elsewhere and often put their former homes on the short-term rental market. It is a snowball effect and the result is a city center alienated from its local residents.

The ministry's approach to housing affordability is also misguided in light of the EU's new initiative. If short-term rentals have significantly driven up housing costs in many European cities, why should things turn out differently here? Are we going to wait until locals take to the streets with water pistols, spraying unsuspecting tourists like they have in Spain?

If we are already seeing signs that the short-term rental market is having a negative impact on housing affordability — and the ministry's own analysis says so, too — then now is precisely the time to create the tools and mechanisms that could help prevent the situation from spiraling out of control.

Enough of this inaction and endless rehashing of analyses. The country's finances, the tourism sector and residents who want a livable environment all need a solution at last. I am not talking about banning anything. Rather, local governments should be given some additional powers, short-term rental apartments should be treated as accommodation establishments and the necessary registry should be created.

World.title: Russia imposes temporary movement restrictions on other side of Estonian border
World.content:
Russia's Federal Security Service (FSB) has imposed temporary movement restrictions in two districts across the border from Estonia.

The border directorate of the FSB's St. Petersburg and Leningrad Oblast branch said measures would be in place in border areas of the Slantsy and Kingisepp districts from September 16–26 to "prevent violations of border and migration regulations" and "protect aquatic biological resources."

During this period, small vessels are prohibited from traveling on the section of the Narva River between the Bolshaya Cheryomukha and Kryusha (Krivasoo) rivers.

A nighttime movement ban has also been imposed outside populated areas within a five-kilometer-wide strip along the state border in the Kingisepp and Slantsy districts. Hunting and carrying firearms are also prohibited in the area.

Andris Viltsin, Estonia's border representative on the Estonian-Russian border, said the Police and Border Guard Board (PPA) had previously been aware that Russia would impose movement restrictions for a certain period in several areas bordering Estonia. The Russian border authorities did not themselves notify the PPA of the restrictions in advance.

The PPA does not consider such restrictions extraordinary.

Viltsin explained that the Russian side has occasionally imposed various movement restrictions as a preventive measure or in connection with exercises and that even under normal circumstances, movement in Russia's border zone is more restricted than elsewhere.

"Russia has significantly stricter measures in place on a daily basis within a five-kilometer-wide area adjoining the border than Estonia does. For example, not everyone can enter Ivangorod (Jaanilinn — ed.) — you need an invitation to do so," Viltsin said.

"The Russian side has imposed measures like these from time to time depending on the situation. It is not routine, but neither is it anything particularly extraordinary," he added.

According to the PPA representative, the Russian side may have been seeking to prevent incidents during the elections.

It recently emerged that Russia is fortifying the bank of the Narva River, although there is no clear link between the two developments.

"It is clearly apparent that the Russian side is increasingly devoting measures and resources to guarding the border in order to make that work more effective and ensure access for a response if necessary. I think this needs to be viewed in the broader context, together with everything else. They are increasing their readiness and capabilities and it seems they have no shortage of resources on that side," Viltsin said.

Russia held sham elections over the weekend, which were won, as expected, by the ruling United Russia party. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has previously warned that Russia plans to mobilize around 300,000 people following the State Duma elections in September.

Interior Minister Igor Taro (Eesti 200) did not rule out the possibility that the restrictions could be connected to a planned mobilization.

"There have certainly been various theories about another round of forced mobilization, and considering the difficulties they have faced in staging their election spectacle, how severe the restrictions they have had to impose have been in order to produce the result they wanted and the kinds of actions they have had to contend with, naturally nothing can be ruled out," he said.

The interior minister noted that not many Russians want to go to war and die and said the measure could be connected to an attempt to prevent citizens from fleeing the country. He also stressed that evading military service is not in itself grounds for receiving international protection.

"Russia itself knows why it is implementing these measures," Taro said. "In any case, they have always had a special regime for the border zone; the area has never simply been freely accessible."

World.title: Estonian households throw away €117 million worth of food a year
World.content:
Estonian households generated nearly 69,200 metric tons of food waste in 2025, with avoidable waste accounting for almost 38 percent of the total, Delfi reports based a new study.

Estonian households generated nearly 69,200 metric tons of food waste in 2025 of which 25,337 metric tons or nearly 38 percent was food loss — food thrown away that could still have been eaten if it had been consumed sooner or stored or handled differently.

This means that nearly 18.5 kilograms of food per person was thrown away over the course of the year. The value of food wasted in households totaled €116.7 million. For an average two-person household, this amounts to a loss of approximately €179 a year, according to a new study on food waste.

Vegetables, prepared foods, dairy products and baked goods accounted for the largest share of food wasted in households. The main causes of avoidable food loss were insufficient planning, a lack of awareness of what was in the refrigerator and preparing excessively large quantities of food.

At the same time, food waste has declined compared with previous years.

Estonia's entire food supply chain generated approximately 139,000 metric tons of food waste in both 2024 and 2025, which amounts to an average of 102 kilograms per person per year. Households accounted for nearly half of the total, but significant amounts of waste were also generated by the food industry, retail, food service and agriculture.

The study was commissioned by the Environmental Investment Center and the Ministry of Climate with support from the EU Cohesion Fund and conducted by Levellab and Roheline Rada.

World.title: Outgoing president awards office chief €11,000 bonus
World.content:
President Alar Karis awarded Krista Zibo, director of the Office of the President, an €11,200 bonus for strong job performance in 2026. Zibo has also received a large bonus in the past.

On January 29 this year, Karis issued a directive setting Zibo's base salary at €6,010 per month. Her previous salary was €5,500. When she took up the post on September 2, 2024, it was €5,000.

On November 24, 2025, Karis decided to award Zibo a bonus of €10,500 for strong job performance.

Zibo also spent nearly two years as director of the Office of the President on a fixed-term arrangement, having been temporarily transferred from the Government Office. As of July 1 this year, just a few months before the new president takes office, she has held the position on a permanent basis.

When ERR asked in early September why the arrangement had only now been changed, the Office of the President said Zibo was needed to ensure stable management and day-to-day operations through the end of Karis' term and during the presidential transition. The response did not explain why this could not have been done under the temporary transfer arrangement.

13 layoffs in 2 years

As of early September, Zibo had laid off 13 employees from the Office of the President over the previous two years. Two employees had their last day at work just about a month before President-elect Ülle Madise was due to take office. One had worked at the office for 26 years and the other for nearly 19 years.

Zibo said the changes were necessary to save money and improve the organization of work.

However, eight people have been hired by the Office of the President over the past two years. The office attributed the new hires to changes in job roles and work processes.

President-elect Ülle Madise has offered the position of director of the Office of the President to longtime senior executive Paavo Nõgene.

World.title: The Estonian helping put a small US town on the art map
World.content:
One of the United States' major art events this summer was the inaugural Medina Art Triennial in New York state where nearly 100 works of art were installed across a town roughly the size of Elva. Karin Laansoo served as the triennial's artistic director.

The broader goal of the event is to revitalize the area around the historic Erie Canal. Completed in 1825, the nearly 600-kilometer-long canal was considered a major feat of engineering at the time. Today, many communities along the canal have fallen into obscurity.

Medina Art Triennial artistic director Karin Laansoo told ETV cultural affairs program "OP" that one of America's largest energy companies was behind the triennial, seeing contemporary art as a way to support the regional economy and attract more tourists.

"Looking back now, we really had no idea just how big, ambitious and complicated this project would become. Nobody knew anything about Medina. I'm not just talking about international artists; I'm talking about people who live an hour away from here. Of the 39 artists, only one had ever been to Medina before because he was born in Buffalo and visited Medina with his father as a child," she said.

Medina's heyday came around the turn of the 20th century. Its prosperity was driven by local sandstone whose quarrying and transportation employed thousands of people, many of them immigrants from Europe.

History teacher Todd Bensley said the triennial is helping put Medina back on the map.

"We have two larger cities around us, Rochester and Buffalo. People may not think about us that much, but when they come here, they enjoy what they see. It's a typical 19th-century American town. Our Main Street is well preserved. There are a lot of great businesses in town. We just have to get people here and they'll fall in love with Medina," he said.

Two buildings more than a century old were restored for the Medina Art Triennial. A former hotel was turned into a visitor center, while an elementary school building that had stood empty for the past 30 years became the main exhibition venue. The latter also features scented works by Estonian artist Kärt Ojavee that seek to convey what Medina smells like.

"Kärt came to Medina last year on a research visit. She spent a week here trying to find the scent that best characterizes Medina. She settled on a particular variety of apple called Honeycrisp. Kärt began extracting different scents from apple blossoms, soil and seeds," Laansoo said.

Susanna Rosenstock, deputy director of the Toronto Biennial of Art, praised the triennial organizers' initiative and said the team had done incredible work.

"It was a major undertaking to bring the exhibits to a small town that perhaps doesn't have the infrastructure needed for exhibitions that would be readily available in a big city. Even though I've only been here for one day, the people and volunteers were very excited and grateful to have this exhibition here. It's unique to Medina and showcases the town's distinctive character. It's different from any other exhibition because it allows you to see the place where you live differently from the way you do in everyday life," she said.

Laansoo said feedback from visitors has been overwhelmingly positive. "The words people use are phenomenal, incredible, life-changing, inspiring," she said, adding that critics have also praised the initiative. "Critics said this new initiative is among the 20 most important art events of 2026."

World.title: Rusafa Integrity Court recovers 51 billion dinars for Rafidain Bank
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Rusafa Investigation Court Specialized in Integrity and Money Laundering Cases announced on Monday, September 21, 2026, the recovery of 51 billion Iraqi dinars on behalf of state-owned Rafidain Bank.

According to an official statement released by the Supreme Judicial Council’s media office and, the restitution was executed following intensive investigative proceedings into major financial and administrative corruption offenses that directly harmed public finances.

The judiciary noted that the successful clawback forms part of an ongoing, systemic anti-corruption drive designed to safeguard state assets, close institutional vulnerabilities, and enforce accountability across the public banking sector.

Rigorous judicial reviews and forensic audit procedures spearheaded by the specialized court enabled authorities to trace the illicitly acquired funds and return the entire 51 billion dinars to state accounts.

Judicial authorities affirmed that legal actions against the implicated perpetrators remain active, emphasizing that prosecutorial teams will continue pursuing individuals and entities employing unlawful mechanisms to generate illicit profits at the expense of public treasury funds.

World.title: Iraq plans to bring 6 million weapons under state control
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – An official in the Iraqi Ministry of Interior said on Monday that the government is proceeding with the decision to restrict the possession of weapons exclusively to security forces.

Hussein al-Awadi, the Undersecretary of the Ministry of Interior, confirmed in a statement that the authorities intend to collect up to six million weapons in the coming months, the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA) reported.

Bringing arms under state control is a decision firmly adopted by the Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces and all Iraqi government security agencies, ensuring that weapons remain exclusively in the hands of official security forces, according to al-Awadi.

In late August, the Iraqi military reaffirmed its commitment to implementing the government’s goal of putting all weapons under state control, stating that it is an irreversible sovereign matter.

Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi is spearheading the government’s proposal to bring all weaponry under strict state control to strengthen national sovereignty, enforce the rule of law, and keep the country out of regional wars.

The effort aims to abolish autonomous armed power by September 30, 2026, when the military mission of the US-led international coalition comes to an end.

Armed factions such as Asaib Ahl al-Haq and Kataib al-Imam Ali have started to sever their autonomous ties to fully integrate into official governmental institutions.

The Iraqi Interior Ministry extended the national weapons registration procedure to the end of 2026 while continuing to purchase medium-range firearms from individuals.

Security personnel are actively targeting unauthorized organizations, carrying out raids and seizing illegal weapons.

Factions such as Kataib Hezbollah, Harakat al-Nujaba, and Kataib Sayyid al-Shuhada refuse to disarm as long as any foreign military presence remains in the country.

While foreign forces depart on September 30, security authorities underline that the date symbolizes the beginning of a progressive, long-term weapon control process, rather than an explicit timetable for final disarmament.

World.title: Iraq urges US firms to accelerate project implementation
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Finance Minister Faleh Sari urged on Saturday US companies operating in the oil and energy sectors to accelerate the implementation of their projects in the country.

Sari remarks took place during his meeting in Baghdad with US Charge d’Affaires to Iraq Steven Fagin to review bilateral relations and discuss approaches to enhance economic and financial cooperation.

The Iraqi minister’s call aims to boost foreign investment and support the development of vital sectors.

Sari said in a statement that Iraq’s relations with other countries are driven by the country’s supreme interests. He emphasized the Iraqi government’s commitment to maintaining a balanced relationship with the United States based on shared interests.

Fagin described the Iraqi government delegation’s visit to Washington last July as highly successful. He emphasized the importance of building upon the visit’s outcomes to strengthen cooperation between the United States and Iraq.

On July 13, Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi paid a five-day visit to the United States, where he signed 48 agreements and memoranda of understanding, as well as announced cooperation between Iraqi and US organizations.

The agreements totaled over $60 billion and encompassed industries such as oil, energy, industry, technology, telecommunications, finance, agriculture, education, and health.

World.title: Spain coach De la Fuente gets new deal after World Cup success
World.content:
Madrid – Spain’s World Cup-winning coach Luis de la Fuente is to sign a new contract keeping him in the role until 2032, the Spanish football federation (RFEF) announced on Monday.

“Luis de la Fuente will extend his contract through the next two European Championships, in 2028 and 2032, as well as the 2030 World Cup,” the RFEF said in a statement.

The 65-year-old, who took charge of Spain in 2022 after replacing Luis Enrique, has since led the national team to World Cup success, Euro 2024 glory and the 2023 UEFA Nations League title.

De la Fuente spent a decade working with Spain’s youth teams before stepping up to the senior role.

“We’re talking about the most successful head coach in the history of the national team, and after fourteen years with us, this is something Luis de la Fuente deserves, a long-term future at the RFEF,” said Rafael Louzan, chair of the Spanish FA’s board of directors.

Spain travel to England on September 26 in their first game since lifting the World Cup in July before hosting Croatia three days later in Seville, to start their Nations League campaign.

They return home to play the Czech Republic in Oviedo on October 3 and end the international window by heading to Croatia three days later.

World.title: EU proposes energy rating for data centres
World.content:
Brussels – Data centres in Europe will be rated on energy and water consumption under an EU proposal put forward Monday to pre-empt possible public discontent as the bloc pushes to boost its computing capacity.

The European Union is aiming to triple its data centre capacity over the next seven years as it plays catch up with the United States and China on artificial intelligence.

“Tripling our data centre capacity cannot mean tripling the pressure on our grids, our water and our energy bills,” said European Commission vice president for clean transition Teresa Ribera.

Data centre construction has sparked backlash across the United States, with local residents often complaining about the power-hungry engines of AI driving up electricity costs — a hot political issue ahead of November’s midterm elections.

The EU said its scheme would provide the public with information about the water and energy consumption of sites with capacity above 500 kW, which already have to report key performance metrics to the EU.

Similarly to that already in use for home appliances, the rating will rank data centres on a coloured scale where A/Green is the most efficient and G/red the least efficient, according to a commission presentation.

To encourage good practices, the score will take into account data centres’ contribution to the grid, such as the reuse of waste heat and the addition of clean energy generation capacities, the commission said.

“Efficient, flexible, powered by additional clean energy and reusing waste heat, this is how data centres become an asset for (the) EU’s energy transition,” Ribera added.

Data centres are yet to become a flashpoint political issue in the 27-nation EU, as the bloc lags well behind the United States on AI development.

The slower growth is in part due to already-high-energy costs, which weigh on European businesses and families alike.

But the International Energy Agency estimates the fast expanding sector will account for more than three percent of overall electricity demand in the EU by 2030.

“To ensure that the digital transformation truly works for our society, we must address the growing energy demand of data centres,” said the EU’s energy commissioner Dan Jorgensen.

“Understanding their energy and resource consumption is the essential first step towards integrating them sustainably into our energy system.”

The labels will be automatically generated by the EU based on companies’ reporting and will be accessible on an EU database, with the first expected to appear in 2027, Brussels said.

The commission said it was also looking into setting minimum performance standards for data centres.

World.title: Putin’s party secures record score in Russia election
World.content:
Moscow – Vladimir Putin’s United Russia party won a record supermajority in the Duma, authorities announced Monday after a tightly controlled three-day election without parties critical of the Kremlin or the war in Ukraine.

Electoral chief Ella Pamfilova said preliminary results showed United Russia — which has dominated Russian politics for 25 years — won 355 of the Duma’s 450 seats.

The result handed Putin’s party an increased supermajority and beat its previous record of 343 seats. The supermajority means it can change the constitution, if it needs to.

The Kremlin said the result of the first parliamentary election since Moscow sent troops to Ukraine in 2022 showed Russians were united around Putin, who has been in power since New Year’s Eve 1999.

The conflict has killed hundreds of thousands, displaced millions and hit ordinary lives in Russia more than ever this year. Moscow has banned criticism of its military campaign and the only party that called for an end to the war was removed from the election.

“These indicators, of course, point to the highest level of consolidation within Russian society around the head of state,” Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told a briefing with journalists.

Elections under Putin are tightly controlled and few in Russia doubted United Russia would win.

Putin had encouraged Russians to vote in support of troops in Ukraine and Moscow also organised voting in occupied Ukraine.

Pamfilova said turnout was over 59 percent, thanking Russians for voting despite what she called “psychological pressure on Russia.”

Russia’s Ukraine campaign broke its ties with the West. Kyiv hit Moscow with its biggest drone attack of the war Sunday, the last day of voting, killing two people and setting an oil refinery ablaze.

“Despite the extreme situation, we were successful in ensuring the maximum security of these elections,” Pamfilova told a Moscow press conference, thanking security services for ensuring the vote went ahead.

– Fifth year of war –

The election result is expected to further tighten Putin’s grip on power.

Some fear a new military mobilisation in Russia. Putin has denied this is in the works, while Kyiv accuses Moscow of planning a callup in coming weeks.

Russia’s Communist party came second in the vote, winning 40 seats. The nationalist LDPR party took 25 seats and the New People party won 20.

The election took place amid the escalation of the Ukraine war in recent months, with no diplomatic solution in sight.

For the Kremlin, it served as a barometer on the mood of Russians towards the war.

In some regions, voting also took place for the heads of regions.

In Chechnya, Ramzan Kadyrov — known for ruling the Muslim-majority republic with an iron fist — won 99.85 percent of the vote, the electoral commission said.

Opposing Kadyrov is hugely dangerous in Chechnya, which is known for extra-judicial killings.

Putin’s political opponents are in exile, prison or dead — such as his main opponents Alexei Navalny who died in an Arctic prison in 2024.

The EU’s top diplomat Kaja Kallas dismissed Russia’s “so-called” election.

“The Kremlin silenced dissent, barred the only registered party that opposed its war in Ukraine, and shut out international election monitors. The veneer of democracy is all that remains in Russia,” Kallas said.

World.title: Iraq’s oil exports hit 35% of shipments leaving Hormuz last week
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Data from Kpler, a leading data platform that tracks commodity flows and maritime shipping, indicates a decline in shipping traffic through the Strait of Hormuz over the past week, with the number of vessels traversing this vital waterway remaining low.

13 oil tankers departed the Strait of Hormuz during the week that started on September 13, carrying a total of approximately 34 million barrels of crude oil.

Saudi Arabia accounted for approximately half of the exports, while Iraq contributed 35 percent of the total crude oil shipments that left the Strait of Hormuz that week.

Shipping traffic through the Strait of Hormuz remains significantly lower than pre-war levels; prior to the outbreak of the war on February 28, the vital waterway typically handled around 125 large commercial vessels daily.oil,

Over the weekend, 12 commodity vessels passed through the Strait of Hormuz, compared to 35 the previous weekend, amid ongoing tensions in the Gulf region and a disagreement between the United States and Iran.

Visible shipping traffic through the strait, which previously served as a conduit for one-fifth of the world’s oil and liquefied natural gas supplies, has decreased significantly. However, Middle Eastern producers continue to export oil on tankers with their transponders switched off.

World.title: Spanish PM says unregulated AI could be ‘devastating’
World.content:
Madrid – Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez on Monday joined a chorus of calls to regulate AI as safety fears around the technology escalate, warning of potentially “devastating” consequences.

The debate over the risks from artificial intelligence has intensified this month, with many of the industry’s leading lights voicing support for more cooperation, regulation and slower development of the technology.

Former employees of major AI companies have resigned warning of the technology’s risks, even pointing to an existential threat to humanity.

“If artificial intelligence is concentrated among a few companies and a handful of countries, its impact on shared prosperity, and therefore on the idea of democracy, will be very negative, if not devastating,” Sanchez told an AI-focused event in Madrid.

“We must act urgently, because unregulated, opaque artificial intelligence running wild… and in very few hands is the perfect recipe for disaster,” added the Socialist leader.

US President Donald Trump — with whom Sanchez has repeatedly clashed — has dismissed fears that AI could wipe out humanity and rejected calls to put greater controls around the fast-moving technology.

Sanchez, an outspoken critic of the power of big tech companies and their bosses, on Monday renewed his criticism of “techno-oligarchs” and urged international coordination on AI.

“Self-regulation does not work”, said Sanchez, calling for an AI “focused on well-being and collective prosperity that enables the building of fairer societies”.

He presented a 12-month plan aiming for “a new social contract for artificial intelligence” in Spain in cooperation with civil society.

This agreement would have to offer “security to people in the face of the changes in work and in life that this technology will entail”, he said.

In February, Sanchez announced a plan to ban social media for under-16s, sparking a spat with X owner Elon Musk and Telegram founder Pavel Durov.

His government has also asked the Spanish prosecutors to investigate X, Meta and TikTok for possible offences related to AI-generated child pornography.

World.title: Grounds in writing a must during arrests even in UAPA: Supreme Court
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Holding that fundamental rights guaranteed under the Constitution cannot be interpreted in a restrictive manner, Supreme Court on Monday held that a person's personal liberty cannot be invaded except in accordance with the procedure established by the Constitution, even if accused of a grave offence and anti-social activities, reports Amit Anand Choudhary.

Elucidating Article 22 of the Constitution, which offers protection against arrest and detention in certain cases, a bench of Justices Ujjal Bhuyan and Atul S Chandurkar said a person must be provided with the grounds of arrest by the probe agency at the time of arrest in writing and its language understandable to the accused. SC said this is applicable in all cases including under special laws - such as PMLA and UAPA - regardless of the nature and gravity of offence.

'Court nod required for re-arrest when flouting Article 22'

Going a step further, the bench said that if a person's arrest is declared illegal for non-compliance with Article 22, then he or she cannot be re-arrested in the same case without approval from a senior police officer and nod from the court concerned.

"We need to remind ourselves that Constitution or a constitutional provision cannot be interpreted in a vacuum. Interpretation of Constitution cannot also be left to imponderables in the form of ifs and buts.





Constitution is based on certain basic principles, much above the statutory threshold. Therefore, violation of Constitution or a constitutional provision cannot be countenanced. It has to be dealt with strictly.

It is not dependent on the nature or gravity of the offence, encompassing within its sweep all offences. It cannot be interpreted in a restrictive manner," the bench said. Referring to SC's verdict in the Prabhu Dayal Deorah case on preventive detention, the court said, "The gravity of the evil to the community resulting from anti-social activities can never furnish an adequate reason for invading the personal liberty of a citizen, except in accordance with the procedure established by Constitution and laws."

The bench said that when a person is arrested, his right to liberty under Article 21 is curtailed and it is necessary that the person must understand on what grounds he has been arrested.

"The requirement of informing the arrested person the grounds of arrest in the light of and under Article 22(1) is not a mere formality but a mandatory binding constitutional safeguard. Thus, if a person is not informed of the grounds of his arrest as soon as may be, it would amount to violation of his fundamental rights thereby curtailing his right to life and personal liberty under Article 21 of Constitution, rendering the arrest illegal," the bench said.

World.title: Animal shelters to cost 7,000 crore, can't build them, NHAI tells SC
World.content:
New Delhi: National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) Monday moved SC seeking to absolve it from the court-assigned responsibility of creating infrastructure along 72,000-km network of national highways (NHs) to shelter stray cattle and animals, which are increasingly causing accidents.

Seeking an urgent hearing on NHAI's application, solicitor general Tushar Mehta asked a bench led by CJI Surya Kant to list it before a special bench headed by Justice Vikram Nath, which had directed NHAI to coordinate with states on removal of stray cattle and animals and keeping them in shelters across India alongside NHs. "Neither does the statute cast such a responsibility on NHAI nor does it have the expertise to create shelters across the 72,000-km stretch of NHs and an additional financial burden of Rs 7,000 crore would be imposed on it in creating and managing these shelters," SG Tushar Mehta said.

Supreme Court

NEW DELHI: Frowning upon grossly inadequate infrastructure and huge vacancies in National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) and appellate NCLAT, Supreme Court Monday said the situation is unacceptable as these two tribunals have to daily deal with Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code matters involving thousands of crores of rupees."They are govt's lifeline now. All nationalised banks, banking sector and all infrastructure projects are also matter of examination before these tribunals only," said a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana after senior advocate Sanjiv Sen on behalf of NCLT Bar Association pointed out that the tribunals' function from dilapidated buildings with poor infrastructure and a large vacancy in the posts of members was hampering adjudication.Sen said leaking roofs, persistent seepage, and the vacancies have severely restricted business hours in the NCLT building in Delhi with most of the benches sitting for half a day. You don't have buildings, you don't have staff, you don't have judgment writers, you don't have proper, adequate technological inclusion."

World.title: Court junks rejection of petition to probe Sonia voter roll entry
World.content:
NEW DELHI: A Delhi court has set aside a 2025 magisterial order rejecting a plea to probe alleged irregularities in the inclusion of Sonia Gandhi's name in the electoral rolls. It observed that the "impugned order suffers from manifest errors in law".

Special judge Vishal Gogne of Dwarka courts remanded the matter to the ACJM for a fresh, reasoned order after an inquiry and after hearing the concerned police officer. It will be listed on Sept 29. He said the order was "non-speaking" and lacked reasons. There was no discussion on the sequence of Sonia's inclusion, deletion and re-inclusion in the electoral rolls of 1980, 1982 and 1983, he said. Advocate Vikas Tripathi's complaint alleged that Sonia's name was unlawfully entered in the electoral roll for New Delhi parliamentary constituency in 1980, before she acquired Indian citizenship.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Her name was allegedly deleted in 1982 and re-entered in 1983, with the complaint claiming the re-entry, too, preceded her acquisition of citizenship on April 30, 1983.

In 2025, ACJM dismissed the complaint as "based on bald assertions unaccompanied by essential particulars of cheating and forgery" and described the material as the "photocopy of the photocopy of the uncertified electoral roll of 1980". Tripathi challenged the order before sessions court in Dec 2025. On Monday, Gogne said such an allegation of "tampering with the electoral rules, fraudulent inclusion of the name of a voter, inclusion of the name of a non-citizen and possible use of false declaration" merits a "reasoned order" on whether cheating and forgery were disclosed.

World.title: No median cuts, surface intersections on future high-speed NH corridors: NHAI
World.content:
A view of the Barapullah Phase-3 elevated corridor that is scheduled to be inaugurated on September 29, 2026, in New Delhi on Saturday. (ANI Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: New access-controlled high-speed national highway corridors will have no median (divider) openings and no at-grade (surface level) intersections, a move that aims at eliminating conflict points and reducing crashes.It has also been mandated under new NHAI guidelines issued on Monday that these corridors wonât have raised concrete dividers but flush medians â painted centre lanes with thick wire ropes or crash barriers. These will also have advance exit signage at 5 km, 2 km, 1 km and 500 metres to help motorists prepare for lane changes well in advance.The design provisions are aimed at improving safety on access-controlled corridors where cars are allowed to travel at speeds of up to 100 kmph. Delhi-Dehradun Expressway, Ambala-Kotputli corridor and Trans-Haryana corridor are among such highways.NHAI said the guidelines seek to bring uniformity in the planning and design of access-controlled high-speed corridors and ensure consistency in technical standards across projects.âThe guidelines will apply to all upcoming four-lane and six-lane greenfield and brownfield access-controlled high-speed national highways,â an NHAI spokesperson said.Officials said eliminating median cuts and surface intersections will prevent dangerous cross movements and wrong-side driving, while standardised signage and geometric design will improve traffic flow and reduce the risk of high-speed crashes on the new generation of national highway corridors.The move is significant as govt has set a target of developing 50,000 km of access-controlled high-speed corridors over the coming years.At present, there are no separate standards governing the planning and design of access-controlled high-speed national highways, except for expressways. The new document fills that gap by laying down dedicated norms for highways that are access-controlled but not classified as expressways.The guidelines also specify lane configuration based on detailed traffic assessment and future traffic projections. Depending on the expected traffic volume and the number of structures such as bridges, flyovers and interchanges, these corridors will have a right of way of 60 metres or 70 metres.

World.title: UP Deputy CM Brajesh Pathak hears public grievances at Janta Darshan
World.content:
During the Janta Darshan, people raised various issues

A large number of people from different districts of Uttar Pradesh reached deputy chief minister Brajesh Pathakâs residence on Monday for a public grievance hearing, or Janta Darshan.The complaints raised during the hearing included issues related to medical treatment, financial assistance, police matters, revenue, family disputes and other administrative concerns.Pathak heard the complaints and contacted the concerned officials over the phone, directing them to take action in accordance with applicable rules and eligibility criteria.He also asked officials to monitor the complaints received during the hearing, track their progress and ensure that action is taken within the stipulated time frame.Pathak directed officials to avoid unnecessary delays in addressing grievances and said complaints should be handled with transparency and accountability.The deputy chief minister also said eligible complainants should receive an appropriate resolution to their grievances and asked officials to ensure that there was no negligence in handling public complaints.

World.title: Uttarakhand CM Dhami says strong cooperatives, M-PACS can strengthen rural economy
World.content:
Uttarakhand CM Dhami says strong cooperatives, M-PACS can strengthen rural economy

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

DEHRADUN: Uttarakhand chief minister Pushkar Singh Dhami on Monday said strengthening cooperatives and M-PACS can play a key role in boosting the rural economy, supporting mountain agriculture and creating opportunities for youth in the state.Virtually addressing the inaugural session of the Shri Laxmanrao Inamdar Second Cooperative Leadership Training Programme at Pantnagar, Dhami stressed the need for skilled leadership to make cooperatives an effective instrument of economic empowerment.The programme was organised by Sahakar Bharati Uttarakhand at Govind Ballabh Pant University of Agriculture and Technology, Pantnagar.Paying tribute to Sahakar Bharati founder Shri Laxmanrao Inamdar on his birth anniversary, CM Dhami said such training programmes would play an important role in strengthening the rural economy by empowering the cooperative sector.He said, "Strong leadership will strengthen M-PACS, strong M-PACS will strengthen villages, and strong villages will make Uttarakhand prosperous."The chief minister said several important initiatives aimed at giving a new direction to the cooperative movement had been launched from Pantnagar, the land of knowledge. The launch of the Sahakar Granth, the Devbhoomi Sarathi initiative of the State Cooperative Federation, new courses in the cooperative sector, a social media reels campaign to connect youth with cooperatives, and the M-PACS leadership training programme would give fresh momentum to the cooperative sector, he said.CM Dhami said the state government is committed to taking Uttarakhand rapidly forward towards the vision of "Samriddhi through Cooperatives".He said cooperatives can serve as an effective means of addressing several challenges faced by the hill state, including migration, strengthening mountain agriculture, providing markets for local products and boosting the rural economy.He said primary agricultural cooperative societies (PACS) are an important pillar of the state's cooperative system and are being strengthened as M-PACS to make them more capable and effective in line with changing requirements.The state government is working to provide better facilities to farmers through M-PACS, create new opportunities for youth and strengthen rural areas economically, he added.The chief minister said skilled and visionary leadership is essential to make M-PACS more effective, and the leadership training programme has been launched with this objective. Training, he said, is not merely a means of enhancing knowledge but also a powerful tool for developing new perspectives, approaches and direction among leaders.CM Dhami said connecting farmers, youth and women with the cooperative movement is a priority of the state government. The government is working to make cooperatives not merely limited to societies, but an effective instrument of public participation and economic empowerment, he said.He called upon the representatives participating in the training programme to further strengthen the spirit of cooperation in their respective areas and encourage more people to join the movement.He said all stakeholders must work together to make cooperatives a people's movement, strengthen villages, create opportunities for youth and enhance the economic strength of farmers.

World.title: The 'chosen one' for a role in BSP is Ishan: Mayawati's latest U-turn in ongoing family drama
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Mayawatiâs chosen one is Ishan Anand. Or is he? Well, at least for now. Thereâs another twist in the ongoing succession drama in the BSP chiefâs family. Younger nephew Ishan, who was ruled out from getting any position in the BSP only ten days back, has ended up winning Mayawatiâs âtrust testâ for a role in the party.

âOnly Shri Ishan Anand from Shri Anand Kumarâs family will now be promoted by giving him a respectable responsibility in the party,â Mayawati announced on X on Sunday.

So, when the BSP holds its national-level meeting in Lucknow on September 23, Ishan is likely to get a ârespectable responsibilityâ in the party. This will be 20 days after his elder brother Akash Anand was shown the door at a similar meeting held on September 3.

Ishan, Akash and their sister Deepika are children of Mayawatiâs younger brother Anand Kumar, who has been âworking in Mayawatiâs service for many years.â

A warning for Ishan

But Ishanâs promotion comes with a strict rider. He has to ârise above attachment to his brothers, sisters and close relatives and work with complete honesty and dedication.â

There was a clear and strong warning for Ishan. âIf he commits any serious act against the party, he too will be shown the door from the party.





But in such a situation, no other member of Shri Anand Kumarâs family will be given any responsibility, big or small, in the party,â Mayawati announced.

Niece loses the race

In a long post on X on September 12, the BSP chief had ruled out any political role for her nephews Akash Anand and Ishan Anand, but left room for Deepika to take on responsibilities in the party if the need arises.

The BSP chief had said, "Today it is my final decision and pledge that in return, none of his sons, in particular, will be allowed to engage in politics by holding any position, big or small, within the BSP.

If Anand Kumar, while remaining with me, needs another member to assist him, then in the current political situation, he can seek the help of his only daughter, Kumari Deepika Anand, who is currently studying law. He can then, based on her honesty, loyalty, and efficiency, assign her his own responsibilities within the party as needed.

"

But that did not happen.

In her post, Mayawati dwelled on the âdilemmaâ she faced in making the decision and also shared the yardstick she used to decide the âchosen one.â

âThe question of who from Shri Anand Kumarâs family I should or should not promote in the party has been a matter of considerable dilemma for me for some time. Bringing this dilemma to an end, and after giving serious thought to every aspect, I have now decided that if any member of his family is to be promoted in the party, it should be someone who does not follow Akashâs footsteps in any way.â

âAs for seeking help from his daughter in the future, after she gets married, if her case also turns out to be like Shri Akash Anandâs, that too would not be in the interest of the party.

Keeping such a possibility in mind, it would now be appropriate in the interest of the party to completely keep Shri Akash Anand and his sister away from being given any responsibility in the party. In other words, there will be no change whatsoever in this decision,â Mayawati wrote in her post.

Doors forever closed for Akash Anand?

Akash Anand, who was groomed for years and, at least on two occasions in the past, announced as Mayawatiâs âpolitical successor,â now seems completely out of the picture.

At least for now.

âOn special request of Shri Anand Kumar, I had to promote his elder son, Shri Akash Anand, in politics. Since his marriage, however, Shri Akash Anandâs conduct and activities at every step have been such that, a few days ago, I once again had to separate him from the party,â Mayawati said in her latest post.

âIn other words, he is now completely caught up in the web of his father-in-law, Shri Ashok Siddharth.

Bringing him back into the party now would amount to a major betrayal of the party, and I can never commit such an act against the party,â she wrote.

Akash Anand's on-off jouney with BSP.

Akash Anand entered politics in 2017 at the young age of 22. Anand, who did his MBA from London, made his political debut with Mayawati at a rally in Uttar Pradesh's Saharanpur, where he shared the dais with Akhilesh Yadav and Ajit Singh.

In April 2019, Akash Anand addressed his first rally in Uttar Pradesh's Agra.

The BSP was then part of the opposition Mahagathbandhan, an anti-Congress and anti-BJP bloc formed in the run-up to the 2019 general election under the leadership of Akhilesh Yadav and Mayawati with Ajit Singh's Rashtriya Lok Dal.

Mayawati appointed him BSPâs national coordinator in June 2019. Since then, it has been a bumpy ride for him. Every promotion since then has been followed by a demotion.

However, now with his younger brother taking the centre stage, it may not be easy for Akash to claw back into the power structure.

The Kanshi Ram reference

The BSP chief shared her mantra for success in politics. âI want to tell the people of the party that, keeping my own experience in mind, if they want to succeed in politics and do something for society, they must, like me, rise above their attachment to their brothers, sisters and close relatives and work with complete honesty and dedication,â Mayawati wrote in the post.

She then referred to the role of BSP founder Kanshi Ram in showing her the path

âThe founder and architect of the BSP, respected Shri Kanshi Ram ji, after entering politics, always kept himself away from giving political benefits to his close relatives and family members.

He allowed them to work in the party organisation only with a selfless spirit. Not only this, he devoted his entire life to the interests and welfare of the âBahujan Samajâ, without creating a family of his own,â Maywati wrote.

âInspired by him, I too decided to follow in his footsteps and devoted my entire life to the âBahujan Samajâ. However, because I am a woman, I was compelled to always keep one of my brothers or sisters with me.

Under this arrangement, my younger brother, Shri Anand Kumar, has been working in my service for many years,â the BSP chief said.

The Ambedkar example

Justifying her move, Mayawati wrote, âI have taken this decision in the interest of the party and the movement, inspired by respected Shri Kanshi Ram ji and influenced by a letter written by the revered Baba Saheb Dr BR Ambedkar.â

The BSP chief stated that Baba Saheb Dr BR Ambedkar had written a letter on February 23, 1956, warning his son Yashwant B Ambedkar over his alleged attempts to try and take control of the Buddhist Bhushan Printing Press.

To convey her message to Ishan and others, Mayawati cited the strong stand taken by Ambedkar against his son, âI have to inform you that I have received several communications from Shri Upsham saying that you are not allowing him to perform his duties as the accountant and cashier of the Buddhist Bhushan Printing Press. You seem to think that by doing this you will take control of the press. I am warning you that the press is public property; it belongs neither to you nor to me, and it is not possible to permit any kind of irregularity in a public account.

Your conduct has not been proper... If you do not heed my final and last instructions, I will remove you from the press and, if you do not heed this warning, I will also prosecute you.â

Road ahead for Ishan

âUneasy lies the head that wears a crownâ: Well, thatâs perhaps how one can describe Ishanâs future in BSP. We will have to wait and see what respectable role he gets from Mayawati on September 23 when the party meets. However, irrespective of the role, the road ahead for Ishan would be challenging.

World.title: CNN, MS NOW, Politico to sue Trump administration over White House access
World.content:
CNN, MS NOW, and Politico will sue the Trump administration after being denied access to the White House, the news outlets said in a joint statement on Monday (September 21, 2026).

President Donald Trump said Friday (September 18) he was banning the outlets from the presidential mansion as punishment for distributing what he calls "fake news."

"This morning, we notified the government that we are filing a lawsuit today to protect our First Amendment rights and defend the principle that the government does not decide what the press reports or publishes," the statement said.

The outlets said the White House revoked their journalists’ credentials “without notice or process” because it “objected to our reporting.”

“Left unchallenged, this threatens press freedom and the public’s right to independent journalism free from government interference,” they said.

Mr. Trump did not detail what prompted the ban but said, “Media outlets shouldn’t be able to constantly write or report FICTION and LIES when they’re covering the President of the United States.”

The 80-year-old Republican — who has long had a fiery relationship with the mainstream media — warned Friday (September 18) that other outlets could face a similar fate but did not say which ones.

CNN had been scheduled to serve Monday (September 21) as the White House TV pool, a rotating assignment in which a broadcaster films on behalf of all television outlets for the day. Updated guidance from the White House late Sunday (September 20) simply listed a back-up crew.

World.title: Trump praises leftist Mamdani after meeting in New York
World.content:
U.S. President Donald Trump heaped praise Monday (September 21, 2026) on New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani as the pair set aside their political differences to discuss immigration enforcement and a multi-billion dollar housing project.

Mr. Trump, a Republican, heavily criticised Mr. Mamdani before he took office in January — calling him "my little communist" and a "total nut job" — but the two men have since struck a surprisingly warm relationship.

"Hopefully, you're going to be a great [mayor]. I'll be able to say you're going to be a great one, and you're off to a start," Mr. Trump told Mr. Mamdani at a news conference.

Their closed-door talks in Manhattan, which lasted around an hour, marked the pair's third public meeting since Mr. Mamdani swept the mayoral election last year.

"We appreciate the president's commitment to the city," Mr. Mamdani said of Trump, who was visiting his hometown New York ahead of the United Nations General Assembly.

The 34-year-old said he expressed his "very strong opinions about how we can keep New Yorkers safe" when asked about Mr. Trump's culling of Temporary Protected Status for thousands of immigrants as part of mass deportation plans.

Mr. Mamdani said they also spoke about a 12,000-home building proposal in New York, which the pair previously discussed in February and would require an estimated $21 billion in federal government funding.

He said he planned to continue cooperating with Mr. Trump, despite acknowledging they have "many disagreements."

"We've both spoken about very different approaches, very different beliefs, and I will continue to have conversations with the president, and frankly with anyone who can deliver relief to the people of this city," Mr. Mamdani said.

Mr. Trump's visit came as top U.S. television networks essentially boycotted coverage of the U.S. President in protest of his decision to ban three outlets, CNN, MS NOW and Politico, from the White House.

Mr. Mamdani said he had told Mr. Trump that all members of the press would be welcome at their joint press conference, held in front of the mayor's official residence.

"That is something that I believe in, is everyone, no matter the opinion or the critique, that we engage," he told reporters.

Mr. Trump, meanwhile, brushed off a suggestion that he had issued the media bans to distract the public from criticism of the war in Iran.

"It's interesting because they [the media] said they were going to boycott me, but they never boycott me, so I wasn't very worried about that," he said.

World.title: BJP wins six of seven mayoral polls in Rajasthan; Congress cries foul
World.content:
After emerging as the largest party in the urban local body elections held recently, the rulingBharatiya Janata Party in Rajasthan on Monday (September 21, 2026) won the mayoral contests in six of the seven major Municipal Corporations. The BJP secured the mayoral posts in Ajmer and Pali despite the Congress securing more seats of councillors in both the towns.

The BJP defeated the Congress in Alwar, Udaipur, Pali and Ajmer, while its candidates were elected unopposed in Bharatpur and Bhilwara. The only consolation for Congress came in Bikaner, where it retained the mayoral post with the election of Anil Kalla.

Of the 309 urban bodies in Rajasthan, elections to the top posts were held in 273 on Monday (September 21). Chairpersons were earlier elected unopposed in some other bodies, while elections in the Jaipur, Jodhpur and Kota Municipal Corporations and Kota district’s Suket municipality will be held on September 25.

Even as the BJP strengthened its position in the urban areas, the Opposition Congress accused the State government of misusing the police and administration to ensure the victory of the ruling party’s candidates. Pradesh Congress president Govind Singh Dotasra said the senior party leaders were subjected to “coercive police action and abusive behaviour”.

Mr. Dotasra alleged that the BJP had used the police force to pressure the Congress councillors and Independents into helping the party form the boards in several towns. Both the BJP and the Congress had moved their councillors to hotels and resorts ahead of voting to prevent poaching and secure the support of Independents.

The Congress suffered a setback in Pali, where it finished third despite emerging as the largest party. BJP candidate Namita Bubukia won the mayoral election with 33 votes, narrowly defeating Congress rebel Rajbala Hingad, who secured 29. The official Congress candidate received only three votes.

In Ajmer, the BJP’s Anamika Sharma was elected mayor with 43 votes, while the Congress received 37 votes. The BJP, whose 32 councillors were elected in the local body polls, secured the support of 11 Independents.

BJP candidate Paras Singhvi was elected mayor in Udaipur, having secured 55 votes, while Suman Lata Agrawal of the party was elected mayor in Alwar. Congress leader Anil Kalla, nephew of former Minister B.D. Kalla, was elected mayor in Bikaner, where the party had won 42 of the 80 wards, crossing the majority mark on its own.

The BJP candidates were elected as heads in 32 of the 47 Municipal Councils and in 162 of the 252 municipalities. The Aam Aadmi Party formed its first Municipal Council board in Baran, while its candidate Sheetal Rathore was elected the chairperson.

The BJP had won 4,182 wards in the urban body polls held on September 9 and 11, while the Congress secured 3,619. Independents and candidates from other parties won 2,273 wards, making their support crucial for the election of heads of several local bodies.

The Congress pointed out that the High Court had to intervene by issuing directives to ensure the safe arrival of Congress and Congress-backed councillors in various urban bodies to cast their votes. The High Court constituted special benches and held hearings late on Sunday night and Monday morning — both days being holidays — to consider urgent petitions seeking protection from arrest for councillors and candidates.

Several councillors and candidates approached the High Court, apprehending arrest in cases registered shortly before the elections. The court granted interim protection from arrest to the petitioners without expressing a final opinion on whether the criminal cases amounted to unlawful interference in the electoral process.

Independent MLA from Hanumangarh, Ganesh Raj Bansal, was arrested by the CID-CB of Rajasthan police on Sunday in connection with a 23-year-old case involving fake land leases. As many as 34 independents backed by Mr. Bansal’s group were elected in the Municipal Council polls. A Judicial Magistrate’s court in Sangaria has remanded Mr. Bansal in police custody till September 25.

World.title: Academicians write to Governor opposing the inter-university transfer of teachers
World.content:
The West Bengal Universities and Colleges (Administration and Regulation) Bill seeks to add one provision in Section 14A of the existing 2017 Act, which will allow inter-university transfer of both teaching and non-teaching employees as and when required, officials said

Several distinguished academics from the State and other parts of the country have expressed concern over the West Bengal Universities and Colleges (Administration and Regulation) (Amendment) Bill, 2026, saying academic productivity will be troubled seriously as the universities will no longer have any teaching, research and institutional autonomy.

The Bill was passed by the West Bengal Assembly on September 10.

In a letter to the Governor R.N. Ravi, who is also the Chancellor of all the universities, a group of 14 academicians said that every university is a distinct institution with its own academic structure, programmes and requirements, and that transferring faculty from one university to another could disturb the academic balance of both institutions.

"To move staff from one institution to another would impair the structural balance of both institutions and hamper their teaching and research programmes. Such programmes cannot be readily revised or interchanged," they stated.

They raised concerns over the ongoing research work across the universities. A university has specialized faculty who attract fresh researchers in that field. Laboratory and library facilities are developed to provide for those special areas. If those faculty members are transferred, young research students would be left without recourse. The material resources would lie unused or underused, they said.

They further pointed out that research funding for the major projects is often linked to the presence of expert faculty members serving as principal investigators. They said interdisciplinary and multi-institutional research projects could be “especially jeopardised” by faculty transfers.

Academics also argued that the development of newer universities should be undertaken through planned recruitment and adequate funding rather than sporadic transfers of teachers from established institutions.

"We are anxious that the new universities should be developed productively, but this cannot be done by sporadic transfer of faculty from elsewhere. At present, all or most of the new universities are grossly lacking in staff, infrastructure and facilities. Some of them have no full-time teachers at all. These needs must be met with due planning and sufficient funding, with extensive recruitment of permanent staff at all levels," the letter read.

They also urged the Governor urged to consider a fundamental issue of academic autonomy.

"All the universities would be brought under centralized administrative control. They could no longer develop freely, each according to its bent. Academic productivity would suffer seriously if university faculty felt they could no longer control their own affairs," they said.

The letter was written, among others, by Professor Emeritus of Jadavpur University Amita Chatterjee, former Palit Professor of Physics, Calcutta University Amitava Raychaudhuri, former IIM Calcutta Economics Professor Anup Sinha, Jadavpur University Raja Ramanna Professor Anupam Basu, former Rabindra Bharati University V.C. Sabya Sachi Basu Ray Choudhury, Tata Institute of Fundamental Research former Director Sabya Sachu Bhattacharya, former Director of Centre for Studies in Social Sciences, among others.

The West Bengal Universities and Colleges (Administration and Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026 was approved by the State Cabinet on September 8. It seeks to add one provision to Section 14A of the existing 2017 Act, which will allow inter-university transfer of both teaching and non-teaching employees as and when required, officials said.

The Bill was tabled by Higher Education Minister Jagannath Chattopadhyay during a special session of the State Assembly.

Addressing the assembly during the tabling of the Bill, Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari said that through the proposed legislation, "so-called pundits" will be sent to newly established institutions that would benefit.

World.title: Mahayuti Minister Mangal Prabhat Lodha is suppressing voice of community members, alleges Jain Monk
World.content:
Jain Muni (monk) Nileshchandra accused State Skill Development Minister Mangal Prabhat Lodha of suppressing the voice of the Jain community in Mumbai over the Dadar Kabutarkhana controversy and warned of a protest if the pigeon-feeding enclosure is not opened in Dadar.

“He is suppressing the voice of the Jain community. I spoke to State Assembly Speaker Rahul Narvekar and told him if the issue is not resolved, I will stage protest outside the Godiji Parshvanath Jain temple in Mumbai’s Paydhuni,” said Muni Nileshchandra.

With his remarks, once again the Kabutarkhana controversy is swelling in Mumbai. It has been demanding the publication of any existing government or municipal policy banning pigeon or bird feeding or immediate clarification that feeding is not prohibited; a regular sanitation programme at feeding areas by the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC); immediate medical and veterinary attention for injured or dehydrated stray animals and birds; protection of cows and all milch and farm animals; and declaration of all ancient temples and sanctuaries as Heritage Sites.

Earlier, the Bombay High Court ordered that pigeon feeding could only be done at four spots suggested by the BMC, including Worli Reservoir, the mangrove area on Lokhandwala Back Road in Andheri West, the Airoli-Mulund check post area and Gorai ground in Borivali West. The timings will be between 7 a.m. and 9 a.m.

The Jain monk disapproved of alternate sites, as these are as far as 4, 5 and even 9 kilometres away, and alleged that the “builders and a few greedy politicians are lobbying for political gains”.

Muni Nileshchandra pointed out why everyone is doing politics on speechless pigeons, saying, “All I want is justice for these innocent animals”. He warned of an indefinite strike if “Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis doesn’t respond to the letter that I am going to write to him in next 15 days”.

Kabutarkhana controversy reached the Bombay High Court after the issue of human deaths due to exposure to pigeon droppings surfaced in July. Shiv Sena leader Manisha Kayande first raised the issue in the Maharashtra Legislative Council on July 3.

World.title: Court orders fresh hearing in Sonia Gandhi’s voter roll entry case
World.content:
A Delhi court on Monday (September 21, 2026) allowed a revision plea challenging a September 11, 2025 Magistrate's order refusing to probe the allegation that Congress leader Sonia Gandhi's name was included in the electoral roll three years before acquiring Indian citizenship in 1983.

Special Judge Vishal Gogne quashed the Magisterial Court's order as "non-speaking". The order had dismissed a complaint filed by Advocate Vikas Tripathi, vice-president of the Central Delhi Court Bar Association of the Rouse Avenue courts.

"The impugned order suffers from a manifest error in law on account of non-compliance with Section 175(3) of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), inter alia, not hearing the submissions of the police officer concerned and non-calling of a status report from the police station concerned," the Judge said.

He said the "non-speaking" nature of the order was evident as the Magistrate did not consider the twin options under law; directing registration of FIR or alternatively, conducting proceedings under BNSS.

The Judge said that the Magistrate, instead of considering the core aspect of whether the complaint disclosed commission of a cognisable offence, digressed towards the issue of citizenship.

The Court remanded the matter back to the Magistrate to pass a reasoned order after hearing fresh arguments.

The matter has been posted for further proceedings on September 29.

World.title: Class 10 girl and boy returning from coaching groped and assaulted in Bihar’s Jamui, sparking a political row
World.content:
Two Class 10 students, a girl and a boy, returning from a coaching class, were allegedly groped and harassed by a group of men in Bihar’s Jamui district on Saturday (September 19, 2026). A video of the incident went viral on social media on Monday (September 21, 2026), prodding the police to register an FIR and arrest three people.

Congress leader Rahul Gandhi and other Opposition leaders said the incident was “deeply disturbing”, indicative of patriarchal attitudes among supporters of the ruling BJP, and exposing the State’s law-and-order situation.

The National Commission for Women on Monday (September 21, 2026) took suo motu cognisance of the alleged assault and harassment, and directed the Director General of Police to immediately file an FIR in the matter. The State Commission for Women also took suo motu cognisance of the incident, and promised that strict action would be taken against those found guilty.

Three arrested so far

“There was no formal complaint registered by anyone against anyone in the incident,” said Jamui Superintendent of Police Vishwajit Dayal. “The police took suo motu cognisance of the incident and approached the victim girl and her friend, a boy. Both were returning from a hillside area after their coaching was over on the Jamui-Lakhisarai road where a group of six to seven people, some even masked, stopped them as it is shown in the viral video and they were being harassed on September 19 evening at around 7 p.m.,” he added.

An FIR (No 428/ 2026) was lodged in the incident at Jamui police station. All the people seen in the viral video were taken into custody and three of them have been arrested. “The police will soon arrest all of those found involved in this unfortunate incident,” Mr. Dayal said.

Register FIR, stop sharing video: NCW

“Any compromise on the dignity, safety, and privacy of women is unacceptable at any level,” said the NCW. The Commission’s chairperson Vijaya Rahatkar wrote to the Bihar DGP, directing him to immediately register an FIR in the incident. The NCW also directed that security, legal assistance, and psychological counselling be provided to the victims, seeking a detailed Action Taken Report in the matter. All necessary legal action should also be taken to stop further sharing of the objectionable video being circulated on social media, the NCW directed.

The Bihar State Commission for Women also took suo motu cognisance of the incident. “I’ve spoken to the Jamui officials, and they detailed to me about the incident as it happened on September 19 evening at 7 p.m. Stern action will be taken against all those found involved in this incident by people having a weird mindset. The Bihar State Commission for Women stands with all such hapless women,” Commission chairperson Apsara said.

‘When control is mistaken for culture’

“The video from Jamui is deeply disturbing,” Mr. Gandhi said in a social media post. “Two class 10 students were stopped on a road. Harassed. Humiliated. Molested. A young girl’s hands folded, begged to be let go while goons groped her and dragged her away. This is not ‘culture’. It is patriarchy: the belief that any man can police a girl’s body, her movement, her choice… When control is mistaken for culture, and such attitudes are normalised by ‘Andhbhakts’, mobs start believing they are the law,” he added.

Demanding prosecution of the culprits under the POCSO Act, Mr. Gandhi, who is also Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha asked, “Who gave these men the right to behave like this? The Bihar government must answer why a girl is not safe on a public road at 7 p.m.?”

Recalling the Jamui and Delhi rape and murder incidents, the Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge too demanded the “harshest punishment for culprits, and accountability from State governments”. Such incidents, he said, “scream to expose the lies and hypocrisy of the BJP’s ‘Nari Shakti Vandan’ and ‘Beti Bachao’ schemes”, meant to empower women.

‘Extremely shameful’

Rashtriya Janata Dal leader Tejashwi Yadav, Leader of Opposition in the Bihar Legislative Assembly, also slammed the State government in a social media post.

“Bihar has been shamed by the BJP-NDA government. Everyone is ashamed. On the Jamui incident, the government’s people are making low-level statements… When the Jamui incident happened, [Bihar Chief Minister] Samrat Choudhary was holding a caste conference,” he noted.

His Singapore-based sister Rohini Acharya said: “The incident in Jamui is extremely shameful and expresses the dire state of law and order under the Samrat government, along with lax administrative influence and the stark reality of policing.” She alleged that the “sisters and daughters of the State are entirely unsafe”.

RJD leader and former MLA Shakti Singh Yadav said, “The law and order situation has completely collapsed in the State, but the government keeps drum beating that women in Bihar today can safely travel even at midnight.”

‘Guilty will be behind bars soon’

State Rural Works Minister Sunil Kumar, said that he too has spoken to the Jamui Superintendent of Police and got all the details about the incident. “All those people allegedly involved into the incident would be behind bars very soon… The Jamui incident even was raked up at the government level,” said Mr. Kumar, who has earlier been a senior police official in the State.

His State Cabinet colleague and Bihar Sports Minister Shreyasi Singh is the BJP MLA from Jamui. “Victims had not filed the FIR, police did it after the viral video and three people have been arrested, the rest too will be arrested…I’m satisfied with the administrative action and hope they will continue to do so.”

(with inputs from Sreeparna Chakrabarty in New Delhi)

World.title: SBSP chief Rajbhar’s claim on U.P. division ignites fresh debate as opposition hit out at NDA
World.content:
Cabinet Minister in the Uttar Pradeshgovernment and Suheldev Bhartiya Samaj Party (SBSP) president Om Prakash Rajbhar on Monday (September 21, 2026) claimed that U.P. will be divided into four parts soon, and the Purvanchal region will get a Chief Minister from the Rajbhar caste; the assertion brought fresh focus on demands for the division of the State.

While the BJP played down the issue, the Congress hit out at Prime Minister Narendra Modi over double-speak, as Mr. Rajbhar referred to his conversation with the PM on the division of the State.

“Once the caste census is completed, there will be no problem in carrying out the division. We will divide the State after the caste census. This is what the Prime Minister of the country said,” said Mr. Rajbhar, a partner of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) in Uttar Pradesh, while addressing a public meeting in Ambedkarnagar district, and referred to his dialogue with Mr. Modi and claimed that the PM told him that the division of the State could happen after the caste census.

Mr. Rajbhar further added, “The day a separate Purvanchal State is created, the first Chief Minister will be a son of the Rajbhar community. When the State is divided, there will be Purvanchal, Madhyanchal, Bundelkhand and Harit Pradesh. The Rajbhar community has the largest vote base in Purvanchal,” he said.

The claim brought fresh focus on demands for the division of the State, as many social and regional outfits pushed for creating states of Purvanchal, Bundelkhand, Harit Pradesh and Madhyanchal.

“The demand for a separate Purvanchal is long pending. We are happy that Om Prakash Rajbhar is raising the issue; the economic and social dynamics of Eastern U.P. are fundamentally different from Western U.P. We hope the demand for division will reach a logical conclusion,” said Devesh Chaubey, who is associated with Purvanchal Vikas Parishad.
